35328.q: What is the school subject in which you learn how votes and elections work called?
35328.e: In civics you learn how Switzerland is governed. That way you are well prepared when you are allowed to have a say later.
35328.m: In civics you learn how politics works.

35329.q: What is it called when you work for others without pay, for example in a club?
35329.e: Many people in Switzerland volunteer in clubs, in the neighbourhood or with the fire brigade. That way they help shape life in the municipality.
35329.m: Voluntary work is helping others without pay.

35330.q: May Swiss women do military service?
35330.e: For Swiss men, service is compulsory. Women may do military service voluntarily and then have the same tasks.
35330.m: In Switzerland women do military service voluntarily.

35331.q: How many years had women had the right to vote at federal level in 2021?
35331.e: Women have been able to vote at federal level since 1971. You work it out like this: 2021 minus 1971 = 50.
35331.m: In 2021, Switzerland celebrated 50 years of votes for women.

35332.q: In which neighbouring country do the second most Swiss abroad live (as of 2024)?
35332.e: Around 101,000 Swiss citizens abroad live in Germany. That puts Germany in second place.
35332.m: Many Swiss abroad live in Germany.

35333.q: Which document can you apply for after naturalisation?
35333.e: After naturalisation you are a Swiss citizen. Then you can apply for a Swiss passport and an identity card.
35333.m: After naturalisation you get the Swiss passport.

35334.q: What can you do with a popular initiative?
35334.e: With a popular initiative, citizens propose a new rule. Then the whole people vote on it.
35334.m: With a popular initiative, the people make a proposal.

35335.e: A popular initiative comes from the people. People who are entitled to vote join together and submit their idea.
35335.m: A popular initiative comes from the people.

35336.q: What does a federal popular initiative change?
35336.e: A popular initiative for the whole of Switzerland aims to change the Federal Constitution. The constitution is the country's most important law.
35336.m: A federal popular initiative aims to change the Federal Constitution.

35337.q: What happens in the end with a valid popular initiative?
a: The Federal Council tears it up
35337.e: When a popular initiative has succeeded, there is a popular vote. Then the voters decide with Yes or No.
35337.m: The people vote on a valid popular initiative.

35338.q: Since when has the popular initiative existed for the whole of Switzerland?
35338.e: The popular initiative at federal level was introduced in 1891. So it is more than 130 years old.
35338.m: The popular initiative has existed in Switzerland since 1891.

35339.q: What do most people mean when they talk about an “initiative” in Swiss politics?
35339.e: In everyday life people often just say “initiative”. They usually mean a popular initiative.
35339.m: Instead of popular initiative, people often just say initiative.

35340.q: Who may vote on a federal popular initiative?
35340.e: Swiss citizens aged 18 and over may vote. They are called voters, or people entitled to vote.
35340.m: The voters vote on a popular initiative.

35341.q: What does a popular initiative show about Switzerland?
a: The people have a big say
Only rich people have a say
35341.e: In Switzerland the people can put forward new ideas themselves. This is called direct democracy.
35341.m: The popular initiative is part of direct democracy.

35342.q: A group collects 10,000 valid signatures every month. After how many months does it have enough for a popular initiative?
35342.e: 100,000 signatures are needed. 100,000 divided by 10,000 is 10, so 10 months.
35342.m: With 10,000 signatures a month, it takes 10 months to reach 100,000.

35343.q: A group has 80,000 valid signatures for an initiative. Is that enough?
35343.e: 100,000 signatures are needed. 100,000 minus 80,000 leaves 20,000 still missing.
35343.m: With fewer than 100,000 signatures, an initiative does not succeed.

35344.q: How do you write “one hundred thousand” as a number?
35344.e: One hundred thousand is a 1 followed by five zeros. That is how many signatures a popular initiative needs.
35344.m: One hundred thousand is written as a 1 with five zeros.

35345.q: What happens to an initiative that has too few signatures at the end of the deadline?
a: The Federal Council pays for the rest
35345.e: If valid signatures are missing at the end of the collection period, the initiative does not succeed. There is then no vote.
35345.m: Without enough signatures, an initiative fails.

35346.e: A year has 12 months. 12 + 6 makes 18, so one and a half years.
35346.m: 18 months are one and a half years.

35347.q: Why do initiatives often collect more than 100,000 signatures?
35347.e: Some signatures are invalid, for example if someone is not entitled to vote. That is why people prefer to collect a few more.
35347.m: People collect extra signatures because some are invalid.

35348.q: What does it mean when an initiative has “qualified”?
a: The people have already said Yes
35348.e: “Qualified” means there are enough valid signatures. Only after that does the vote follow.
35348.m: An initiative has qualified when there are enough valid signatures.

35349.q: May you also submit a popular initiative with 150,000 signatures?
35349.e: At least 100,000 valid signatures are needed. More signatures are allowed.
35349.m: For an initiative, 100,000 signatures are the minimum.

35350.q: What do you sign for a popular initiative?
35350.e: For an initiative you sign a list called the signature form. The municipality then checks every signature.
35350.m: For an initiative you sign a signature form.

35351.q: What do you write on the signature form next to your signature?
35351.e: The form asks for surname, first name and address. Then comes your own signature.
35351.m: The signature form has your name, address and signature.

35352.q: What text is at the top of an initiative's signature form?
a: Title and text of the initiative
35352.e: The form shows the title and the exact text of the initiative. That way you know what you are signing for.
35352.m: The form says what you are signing for.

35353.q: Which date must you give on the signature form?
a: The date of your dentist appointment
35353.e: On the form you give your date of birth. This lets the municipality check who has signed.
35353.m: The signature form includes your date of birth.

35354.q: Who may sign on the same signature form?
a: People from all over the world
35354.e: Only people from the same political municipality may sign on one form. The municipality then checks its own residents.
35354.m: A signature form is for one single municipality.

35355.q: Who checks on the form whether someone is entitled to vote?
35355.e: The municipality where the person lives checks that they live there and may vote. It confirms this on the form.
35355.m: The municipality confirms that someone is entitled to vote.

35356.q: How must you sign the form?
35356.e: Each person must sign themselves, by hand. Nobody may sign for someone else.
35356.m: Everyone signs the form themselves, by hand.

35357.q: How often may you sign for the same initiative?
35357.e: Each person may sign only once for the same initiative. Double signatures are invalid.
35357.m: You sign only once for the same initiative.

35358.q: Where do people often collect signatures for an initiative?
35358.e: Many collectors stand in squares and streets. There they talk to people and ask for a signature.
35358.m: Signatures are often collected in the street.

35359.q: What do signature collectors in the street usually have with them?
35359.e: To collect signatures you need signature forms and something to write with. Often there is also a small stand.
35359.m: Collectors have forms and a pen with them.

35360.q: Do you have to sign when a collector asks you?
a: Yes, or you get a fine
35360.e: Signing is voluntary. If you do not agree with the idea, you can simply say no.

35361.q: Apart from in the street, how else can you get a signature form?
a: Collect it from the lost property office
35361.e: Many committees put their forms online. You print the form, sign it and post it back.
35361.m: You can often print a form from the internet.

35362.q: May a 9-year-old child sign a federal initiative?
35362.e: Only people entitled to vote may sign. In Switzerland you are entitled to vote from the age of 18.
35362.m: You may sign an initiative from the age of 18.

35363.q: What is forbidden when collecting signatures?
35363.e: Anyone who forges signatures commits a crime. Every signature form also points this out.

35364.q: Why do collectors explain their idea to people?
a: So they sign because they are convinced
35364.e: People who understand an idea and like it are more likely to sign. That is why collectors briefly explain what it is about.
35364.m: Collectors explain their idea so people are happy to sign.

35365.q: What do you do with the completed signature form?
35365.e: The completed form goes back to the committee. Only then can the signature be counted.
35365.m: You send a completed form back to the committee.

35366.q: What can you achieve with a referendum?
35366.e: With a referendum you demand that the people vote on a new law. Then the people decide whether it applies.
35366.m: With a referendum, the people vote on a law.

35367.q: Who makes the laws in Switzerland that you can challenge with a referendum?
35367.e: The Federal Assembly is the Swiss parliament. It passes new laws, and a referendum is possible against them.
35367.m: Parliament makes laws, and the people can check them with a referendum.

35368.q: Which referendum always takes place without signatures?
35368.e: If the Federal Constitution changes, the people must always vote. This is called a mandatory referendum.
35368.m: When the constitution changes, the people always vote.

35369.q: What does the word “optional” mean in the optional referendum?
35369.e: “Optional” means it only happens if someone demands it. This requires signatures.
35369.m: An optional referendum only happens if someone demands it.

35370.q: Who can demand a referendum against a federal law?
a: Only the President of the Confederation
35370.e: A referendum can be demanded by 50,000 voters or 8 cantons. Usually groups collect signatures.
35370.m: Voters or cantons can demand a referendum.

35371.q: Which referendum only happens if enough signatures are collected?
35371.e: In an optional referendum, a vote only takes place if 50,000 voters or 8 cantons demand it. Optional means voluntary.

35372.q: Are there referendums in cantons and municipalities too?
35372.e: Cantons and many municipalities also have the referendum. The rules and numbers of signatures vary there.
35372.m: Referendums exist at federal level, in cantons and in municipalities.

35373.q: What happens to a new law if nobody launches a referendum?
35373.e: If no referendum succeeds within the deadline, the law simply applies. There is then no vote.
35373.m: Without a referendum, a new law comes into force.

35374.q: What is it called when at least 8 cantons demand a popular vote on a federal law?
35374.e: Cantons can also demand a referendum. The cantonal referendum has only succeeded once so far, in 2003 against a federal tax package.
35374.m: At least 8 cantons can demand a cantonal referendum.

35375.q: A referendum needs 50,000 signatures in 100 days. How many is that on average per day?
35375.e: 50,000 divided by 100 is 500. So you have to collect about 500 signatures every day.
35375.m: A referendum needs an average of 500 signatures a day.

35376.q: From when does the 100-day deadline for a referendum run?
a: From the publication of the law
From the start of the next session
35376.e: The collection period begins when the new law is published in the Federal Gazette. From then on the days count.
35376.m: The referendum deadline begins with the publication of the law.

35377.e: 100,000 divided by 2 is 50,000. That is how many signatures a referendum needs.

35378.e: An initiative needs 100,000 signatures, a referendum 50,000. So the initiative needs more.
35378.m: An initiative needs more signatures than a referendum.

35379.q: A referendum has 60,000 valid signatures. Has it qualified?
35379.e: A referendum needs 50,000 signatures. 60,000 is more, so it is enough.
35379.m: With at least 50,000 signatures, a referendum qualifies.

35380.q: A committee has 45,000 valid signatures for a referendum. How many are missing?
35380.m: A referendum needs at least 50,000 signatures.

35381.q: How long do you have to collect signatures for a referendum?
35381.e: For a referendum you only have 100 days, a little over three months. For a popular initiative it is 18 months.
35381.m: The collection period is shorter for a referendum than for an initiative.

35382.q: Who establishes whether a referendum against a federal law has enough signatures?
35382.e: The signatures for a referendum go to the Federal Chancellery. It checks whether there are enough valid ones.
35382.m: The Federal Chancellery also checks the signatures for a referendum.

35383.q: Which area does a federal popular initiative apply to?
35383.e: “Federal” means it concerns the whole of Switzerland. Such an initiative wants a rule for the entire country.
35383.m: A federal initiative applies to the whole of Switzerland.

35384.q: Can a citizen entitled to vote bring an idea for the whole country to a vote?
a: No, only the Federal Council may
Only as a member of parliament
35384.e: With a popular initiative, any person entitled to vote can put forward an idea. They need a committee and enough signatures.
35384.m: With enough signatures, anyone entitled to vote can put forward an idea for the whole country.

35385.q: Which majorities does a federal popular initiative need?
35385.e: A federal initiative needs a Yes from the majority of the people and the majority of the cantons. This is called the popular majority and the cantonal majority.
35385.m: An initiative needs the popular majority and the cantonal majority.

35386.q: What is the popular initiative for a single canton called?
35386.e: There are popular initiatives in the cantons too. They are called cantonal popular initiatives and apply only to that canton.
35386.m: A cantonal popular initiative applies to one canton only.

35387.q: How many topics may a popular initiative cover?
35387.e: An initiative must respect the unity of subject matter. It may only deal with one topic, otherwise parliament can declare it invalid.
35387.m: A popular initiative may only deal with one topic.

35388.q: What was the first federal popular initiative to be accepted?
a: The ban on slaughter without stunning, 1893
35388.e: In 1893 the people accepted their first initiative: a ban on slaughtering animals without stunning them first.
35388.m: The first accepted popular initiative was the 1893 ban on slaughter without stunning.

35389.q: How often does a federal popular initiative get through with the people?
35389.e: Most federal popular initiatives are rejected. Only a small share is accepted.
35389.m: Most popular initiatives are rejected by the people.

35390.q: Where is an accepted federal popular initiative written down?
35390.e: If an initiative is accepted, its text goes into the Federal Constitution. Afterwards parliament often makes matching laws.
35390.m: An accepted initiative goes into the Federal Constitution.

35391.q: What is an optional referendum for?
a: Being able to reject a law
35391.e: With an optional referendum, the people can reject a new law. First, enough signatures are needed.
35391.m: With a referendum, the people can reject a law.

35392.q: In a referendum, the majority of the people say No. What happens to the law?
a: It does not come into force
35392.e: If the majority say No, the law is rejected. It then does not come into force.
35392.m: After a No, the law does not come into force.

35393.q: What can an association do if it does not like a new federal law?
35393.e: Anyone who opposes a new law can collect signatures and launch a referendum. Then the people decide.
35393.m: You can launch a referendum against an unpopular law.

35394.q: Who often collects signatures against a new law?
35394.e: Often it is parties, associations or groups of citizens. They do not agree with the law.
35394.m: Parties or associations often collect signatures against a law.

35395.q: In an optional referendum, does a federal law also need a Yes from the majority of the cantons?
a: No, the popular majority is enough
Yes, it needs people and cantons
Yes, but only the large cantons
35395.e: In an optional referendum the majority of voters decides. The cantonal majority is not needed there.
35395.m: In an optional referendum only the popular majority counts.

35396.q: In a referendum, what does a “Yes” on the ballot paper mean?
a: I do not want the law
I want parliament to discuss it again
35396.e: In the vote, the question is whether you want to accept the law. So a Yes means the law should apply.
35396.m: A Yes in a referendum means the law should apply.

35397.q: When do you launch a referendum?
35397.e: First parliament passes a law. Only after that can you launch a referendum against it.
35397.m: You launch a referendum after parliament has passed a law.

35398.q: What is the group that organises a referendum called?
35398.e: Anyone who launches a referendum usually forms a referendum committee. It organises the collection of signatures.
35398.m: A referendum committee organises the campaign against a law.

35399.q: Which language does the word “petition” come from?
35399.e: “Petition” comes from the Latin word “petitio”. It means a request or plea.
35399.m: The word petition comes from Latin and means request.

35400.q: Can you also collect a petition on the internet?
35400.e: There are no strict formal rules for a petition. That is why many petitions are collected online today.
35400.m: You can also collect a petition online.

35401.q: What is the minimum number of signatures a petition needs?
35401.e: There is no fixed number for a petition. Even a single person can submit a petition.
35401.m: A petition does not need a particular number of signatures.

35402.q: Does a petition lead to a popular vote?
35402.e: A petition is a request. It does not lead to a popular vote like an initiative does.
35402.m: A petition does not lead to a popular vote.

35403.q: A class would like a zebra crossing in front of the school. What can it do?
35403.e: With a petition, even a school class can send a wish to the municipality. You do not have to be entitled to vote for this.
35403.m: With a petition, even a school class can express a wish.

35404.q: Where is the right to submit a petition written down?
35404.e: The right of petition is in the Federal Constitution, in Article 33. It is one of the fundamental rights.
35404.m: The right of petition is in the Federal Constitution.

35405.q: What must an authority at least do with a petition?
35405.e: The authority must read the petition and take note of it. But it does not have to carry out the wish.
35405.m: An authority must take note of a petition.

35406.q: May you also address a petition to your own municipality?
35406.e: You can address a petition to many authorities: the municipality, the canton or the Confederation.
35406.m: A petition can go to the municipality, the canton or the Confederation.

35407.q: May someone be punished for signing a petition?
35407.e: The Federal Constitution protects everyone who submits a petition. Nobody may suffer any disadvantage because of it.
35407.m: Anyone who signs a petition must not suffer any disadvantage.

35408.q: Where do you submit the signatures for a federal popular initiative?
35408.e: You submit the signatures for a federal initiative to the Federal Chancellery in Bern.
35408.m: The signatures for an initiative go to the Federal Chancellery.

35409.q: In which city is the Federal Chancellery?
35409.e: The Federal Chancellery is in Bern, where the Federal Council and parliament also work.
35409.m: The Federal Chancellery is in Bern.

35410.q: What does the Federal Chancellery do with the submitted signatures of a popular initiative?
a: It gives them to the Federal Supreme Court
It sends them back to the committee
35410.e: The Federal Chancellery checks and counts the signatures. Then it says whether the initiative has qualified.
35410.m: The Federal Chancellery counts the signatures.

35411.q: Who checks the signature form of a popular initiative before collection begins?
35411.e: Before collection, the Federal Chancellery checks the form and the title. That way the format is right from the start.
35411.m: Before collection, the Federal Chancellery checks the form.

35412.q: Who does the Federal Chancellery mainly work for?
35412.e: The Federal Chancellery is the Federal Council's staff office. It helps the Federal Council with its work.
35412.m: The Federal Chancellery works for the Federal Council.

35413.q: What does the Federal Chancellery check about the title of an initiative?
35413.e: The title of an initiative must not be misleading or contain advertising. Otherwise the Federal Chancellery changes it.
35413.m: The title of an initiative must not be misleading.

35414.q: Which signatures does the Federal Chancellery count in the end?
35414.e: Only valid signatures count. Duplicate or invalid signatures are not counted.
35414.m: The Federal Chancellery only counts valid signatures.

35415.q: Where does the Federal Chancellery announce that an initiative has qualified?
a: In the canton of Bern's official gazette
35415.e: The Federal Gazette is the Confederation's official publication. It states whether an initiative has enough valid signatures.
35415.m: The Federal Chancellery publishes its decisions in the Federal Gazette.

35416.q: What is the group that starts a popular initiative called?
35416.e: A popular initiative is started by an initiative committee. It is responsible for the initiative.
35416.m: An initiative committee starts a popular initiative.

35417.q: What is the minimum number of people in an initiative committee?
35417.e: An initiative committee consists of at least 7 people entitled to vote. These people are responsible for the initiative.
35417.m: An initiative committee has at least 7 members.

a: A group that starts a popular initiative
A commission of the Federal Council
A party in the Council of States
35418.e: The initiative committee is the group of voters who launch a popular initiative. It organises the collection of signatures.
35418.m: An initiative committee starts a popular initiative.

35419.q: Who may take part in an initiative committee?
a: All residents, even without a Swiss passport
Only members of the National Council
Only members of a municipal government
35419.e: The members of the initiative committee must be entitled to vote. That means Swiss citizens aged 18 and over.
35419.m: Only people entitled to vote sit on the initiative committee.

35420.q: How many months does an initiative committee have to collect the signatures?
35420.e: From publication in the Federal Gazette, the committee has 18 months. In this time it needs 100,000 valid signatures.
35420.m: You have 18 months for a popular initiative.

35421.q: Why are the names of the initiative committee on the signature form?
a: So you can see who started the initiative
So these people do not have to sign
Because only they may count signatures
So they can join the Federal Council later
35421.e: The form shows the names of the committee members. That way you know who is behind the initiative and who may also withdraw it.
35421.m: The form shows who started the initiative.

35422.q: What does the initiative committee often do before the vote?
35422.e: The committee wants its initiative to be accepted. That is why it advertises with posters and leaflets.
35422.m: An initiative committee campaigns for its initiative.

35423.q: What does an initiative committee do first?
a: It writes the text of the initiative
It submits the initiative in Bern
35423.e: At the start, the committee writes down exactly what the initiative wants. Then the text is checked, and only after that are signatures collected.
35423.m: An initiative committee first writes the text of the initiative.

35424.q: How does the initiative committee decide on a withdrawal?
a: By a majority of the members
35424.e: A withdrawal needs the agreement of the majority of the committee members. One person alone cannot decide.
35424.m: The majority of the committee decides on a withdrawal.

35426.q: Who makes a counter-proposal to a federal popular initiative?
35426.e: The counter-proposal is made by the Federal Assembly, that is parliament. It often goes a little less far than the initiative.

35427.q: Can you vote Yes twice for an initiative and a direct counter-proposal?
35427.e: Since a vote in 1987, you may say Yes to both proposals. This is called the double Yes.
35427.m: For an initiative and a counter-proposal, you may say Yes twice.

35428.q: What is the extra question called when an initiative and a counter-proposal are put to the vote?
35428.e: In the deciding question you say which you would prefer if both are accepted. That way there is a clear result in the end.
35428.m: With the deciding question you choose between the initiative and the counter-proposal.

35429.q: Why does parliament sometimes make a counter-proposal?
a: The initiative goes too far for it
The initiative has too few signatures
The Federal Council demands it for every initiative
35429.e: Sometimes parliament likes the idea but finds the initiative too strict. Then it makes a milder counter-proposal.
35429.m: A counter-proposal is often milder than the initiative.

35430.q: Must parliament always make a counter-proposal?
a: Yes, but only for big initiatives
Only if the cantons demand it
35430.e: A counter-proposal is voluntary. Often an initiative goes to the vote without a counter-proposal.

35432.q: What can the committee do if it likes the counter-proposal?
35432.e: If the committee likes the counter-proposal, it can withdraw its initiative. Then there is no vote on the initiative.
35432.m: If the counter-proposal is good, a committee sometimes withdraws its initiative.

35433.q: What is a counter-proposal called that is put to the vote at the same time as the initiative?
35433.e: A direct counter-proposal also changes the constitution. That is why the initiative and the counter-proposal are voted on on the same day.
35433.m: A direct counter-proposal is voted on together with the initiative.

35434.q: What does the right to education mean?
35434.e: The right to education says that all children may learn and go to school. That way they can shape their lives well later on.
35434.m: Every child has the right to learn.

35435.q: According to children's rights, what should countries encourage so that children learn a lot?
a: Holidays that are as long as possible
35435.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child requires countries to encourage regular school attendance. This should mean fewer children leave school too early.
35435.m: If you go to school regularly, you can learn a lot.

35436.q: What do children in Switzerland get if they hardly speak any German yet?
35436.e: Many Swiss schools offer lessons in German as a second language. That way all children can keep up with their learning.
35436.m: With German lessons, all children can keep up at school.

35437.q: According to children's rights, what should school develop in every child?
35437.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child says that education should fully develop each child's personality and talents.
35437.m: School should develop every child's talents.

35438.q: According to children's rights, what should children also learn to respect at school?
35438.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child also names respect for the natural environment as an aim of education.
35438.m: At school, children also learn to respect nature.

35439.q: According to children's rights, what should school encourage in children?
35439.e: Education should prepare children for a life of peace and mutual understanding. This is in the Convention on the Rights of the Child.
35439.m: Good education encourages peace and friendship.

35440.q: What may teachers not do at school?
35440.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child requires school discipline to respect the child's dignity. Hitting is forbidden in Swiss schools.
35440.m: Children's dignity must be respected at school too.

35441.q: Which young woman from Pakistan fights for all girls to be allowed to go to school?
35441.e: Malala Yousafzai has campaigned since she was a child for all girls to be allowed to learn. For this she received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, at the age of 17.
35441.m: Malala fights for all girls to be allowed to learn.

35442.q: According to children's rights, what should children get so they can find a suitable job?
35442.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child requires educational and careers guidance to be available to all children. In Switzerland there are careers advice centres for this.
35442.m: Careers advice helps young people find the right job.

35443.q: Which children's right allows you to play with friends after school?
35443.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child gives every child the right to play and leisure. So playing is not just fun, it is a right.

35444.q: According to children's rights, what is also part of the right to leisure?
35444.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child names the right to rest, leisure, play and relaxation together. Children need breaks to recharge.
35444.m: Children have a right to rest and relaxation.

35445.q: According to children's rights, what may children take part in freely?
35445.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child gives children the right to take part in cultural and artistic life, for example in concerts, festivals or museums.
35445.m: Children may take part in art and culture.

35446.q: Which activity is part of the right to art and culture?
35446.e: Acting in a play is an artistic activity. Children's rights allow children to express themselves artistically.
35446.m: Theatre, music and painting are part of culture.

35447.q: Why is playing so important for children?
a: Children learn a lot from it
35447.e: When they play, children practise movement, imagination and getting along with others. That is why playing is important for their development.
35447.m: Children learn a great deal through play.

35448.q: Where can children in many Swiss municipalities borrow games and toys?
35448.e: A toy library (ludothèque) is a kind of library for games. You can borrow games and toys there for little money.
35448.m: You can borrow games at the toy library.

35449.q: According to children's rights, who should promote leisure activities for children?
35449.e: According to the Convention on the Rights of the Child, countries must promote good and equal opportunities for leisure, culture and recreation.
35449.m: The state should promote good leisure activities for children.

35450.q: Which children have a right to play?
35450.e: The right to play applies to every child in the world, no matter where they live or how well they do at school.

35451.q: What did the UN create its own international day for in 2024?
35451.e: The UN declared 11 June the International Day of Play. It is a reminder of how important play is for children.
35451.m: 11 June is the International Day of Play.

35452.q: According to children's rights, what does a sick child have?
35452.e: The right to health means that sick children are treated by doctors.
35452.m: Sick children have a right to medical help.

35453.q: According to children's rights, what should countries provide for all children so they stay healthy?
35453.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child requires children to get clean drinking water and healthy food. Dirty water can make you ill.
35453.m: Clean drinking water is important for health.

35454.q: What protects children from dangerous diseases such as measles?
35454.e: Vaccinations help the body to fight diseases such as measles. They are part of health care for children.

35455.q: Who often checks schoolchildren's teeth in Switzerland?
35455.e: Many Swiss municipalities have a school dental service. It regularly checks schoolchildren's teeth.
35455.m: The school dentist helps keep children's teeth healthy.

35456.q: According to children's rights, what should children learn about health?
35456.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child says that parents and children should get knowledge about health, nutrition and hygiene.
35456.m: If you know about health, you can look after yourself better.

35457.q: A child has a high fever and may go to the doctor. Which right is that?
35457.e: When a child is ill, they are entitled to treatment. That is part of the right to health.
35457.m: Being allowed to go to the doctor is part of the right to health.

35458.q: According to children's rights, what must children be specially protected from?
35458.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child requires children to be protected from the use of drugs. Drugs harm the body and the brain.
35458.m: Children must be protected from drugs.

35459.q: Which habit protects children from many diseases?
35459.e: Washing your hands with soap removes many germs. The Convention on the Rights of the Child says children should get knowledge about hygiene.
35459.m: Washing your hands protects against diseases.

35460.q: What is the name that a child shares with their family called?
35460.e: The surname, also called the family name, shows which family a child belongs to. The first name, on the other hand, belongs only to the child.
35460.m: The surname links a child to their family.

35461.q: Where is a child's birth registered in Switzerland?
35461.e: The civil registry office enters births, names and parents in a register. That way the child is officially known.
35461.m: The civil registry office records every birth.

35462.q: According to children's rights, what does a child get as well as a name?
35462.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child gives every child the right to a name and a nationality. So they belong to a country.
35462.m: Every child has a right to belong to a country.

35463.q: Who normally chooses a baby's first name in Switzerland?
35463.e: In Switzerland, parents choose their child's first name. The civil registry office then records it.
35463.m: Parents choose their child's first name.

35464.q: According to children's rights, whom does a child have the right to know, as far as possible?
35464.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child says that a child has the right, as far as possible, to know their parents.
35464.m: Children have the right to know their parents.

35465.q: What is part of a child's identity, which the state must protect?
35465.e: According to the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the state must protect the child's identity. This includes name, nationality and family.
35465.m: Name and family are part of a child's identity.

35466.q: Which document from the civil registry office shows a child's name and date of birth?
35466.e: The birth certificate is an extract from the civil status register. It shows name, date of birth and place of birth.
35466.m: The birth certificate shows who a child is and when they were born.

35467.q: What is the name that only you have, not your whole family?
35467.e: Each child gets a first name of their own. They share their surname with their family.
35467.m: My first name belongs only to me.

35468.q: What does the right to a family mean?
a: Children may grow up with their parents
Children may not have brothers or sisters
35468.e: According to the Convention on the Rights of the Child, children should not be separated from their parents against their will. Family is very important for children.
35468.m: Children have the right to grow up with their family.

35469.q: When may a child be separated from their parents?
a: When it is necessary for their wellbeing
When they do not like vegetables
35469.e: Separation is only allowed when it is necessary for the child's wellbeing, for example if they are not safe at home.
35469.m: A child may only be separated from their parents to protect them.

35470.q: What may a child do if their parents live apart?
35470.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child says that a child may have regular contact with both parents, unless this harms them.
35470.m: Children may see both parents, even if they live apart.

35471.q: According to children's rights, who is jointly responsible for bringing up a child?
35471.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child says that mother and father are jointly responsible for the child's upbringing and development.
35471.m: Mother and father are jointly responsible for their child.

35472.q: Where can a child live if they cannot stay with their parents?
35472.e: According to children's rights, children without a family are entitled to special protection. A foster family can give them a new home.
35472.m: A foster family looks after children who cannot live with their parents.

35473.q: What is it called when a child is taken into a new family for ever?
35473.e: In an adoption, new parents legally become the child's parents. Children's rights require the child's wellbeing to come first.
35473.m: With adoption, a child gets new parents for ever.

35474.q: What should countries do if a family is separated in different countries?
a: Help it to come back together
Send the children to a home
35474.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child requires applications for family reunification to be dealt with positively and quickly.
35474.m: Separated families should be allowed to come back together.

35475.q: Who advises parents in Switzerland on questions about babies and toddlers?
a: The parent and child advice service
35475.e: The parent and child advice service helps parents free of charge with questions about feeding, sleep and the development of their young children. According to children's rights, the state should support parents in this way.
35475.m: The parent and child advice service supports young families.

35476.q: What does the right to food mean?
a: Every child should be able to eat enough
35476.e: The right to food means that every child should get enough healthy food to grow and stay healthy.
35476.m: Every child has the right to enough to eat.

35477.q: Who must first make sure that a child has enough to eat?
35477.e: According to the Convention on the Rights of the Child, the parents are first responsible for making sure their child can live well. That includes enough food.
35477.m: Parents are first to provide food for their children.

35478.q: Who helps in Switzerland when parents do not have enough money for food?
35478.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child says that the state helps families, especially with food, clothing and housing. In Switzerland, social assistance does this.
35478.m: Social assistance supports families in need.

35479.q: What is at the very bottom of the Swiss food pyramid?
35479.e: In the Swiss food pyramid, unsweetened drinks such as water are at the very bottom. You need more of these than anything else every day.
35479.m: Drinking water is the basis of a healthy diet.

35480.q: What is it called when a child gets too little or the wrong food for a long time?
35480.e: With malnutrition, the body lacks important nutrients. The Convention on the Rights of the Child requires countries to fight it.
35480.m: Malnutrition makes children weak and ill.

35481.q: What is the first food for many babies?
35481.e: Many babies drink breast milk first. According to the Convention on the Rights of the Child, parents should be informed about the advantages of breastfeeding.
35481.m: Breast milk is the first food for many babies.

35482.q: Why do some children in the world not have enough to eat?
a: Because of holidays that are too long
35482.e: Poverty, war and drought are important causes of hunger. That is why help is needed so that the right to food applies to everyone.
35482.m: Poverty and war are common causes of hunger.

35483.q: Which drink is the best thirst quencher for children?
35483.e: Water has no sugar and quenches thirst best. Sugary drinks damage your teeth.
35483.m: Water is the best thirst quencher.

35484.q: What does the right to a home mean?
a: Children should be able to live safely
Children live in the school building
35484.e: Every child needs a safe place to live, sleep and spend their life. This is part of an adequate standard of living.
35484.m: Every child needs a safe home.

35485.q: According to children's rights, what should children have enough of besides food and housing?
35485.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child names food, clothing and housing as things the state should help families with.
35485.m: Every child needs food, clothing and housing.

35486.q: Which children need special protection because they had to flee their country?
35486.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child says that refugee children must get suitable protection and help, including somewhere to stay.

35487.q: What are children called who have to live on the street?
35487.e: Street children have no home and sleep outside. There are many such children in the world, even though every child has a right to a home.
35487.m: Street children have no safe home.

35488.q: Where do some children live who cannot live with their family?
35488.e: A children's home offers children a home with care when they cannot live with their family.
35488.m: A children's home can give children a safe home.

35489.q: What are children called who flee to a foreign country without their parents?
35489.e: Unaccompanied minors are children and young people who flee without their parents. In Switzerland they get accommodation and care.
35489.m: Children who flee alone need especially strong protection.

35490.q: According to children's rights, what standard of living should children have?
35490.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child gives every child the right to an adequate standard of living. That means they have enough to live on, including a home.
35490.m: Every child should have enough to live on.

35491.q: What can suddenly take a family's home away?
35491.e: Natural disasters such as earthquakes or floods can destroy houses. Then families quickly need help and somewhere to stay.
35491.m: After a disaster, families quickly need a new roof over their heads.

35492.q: What does the right to equal treatment mean?
a: All children must look the same
All children wear the same clothes
All children have the same marks
35492.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child says that the rights apply to every child without distinction. Nobody may be disadvantaged.
35492.m: Children's rights apply equally to all children.

35493.q: May a child be treated worse because of the colour of their skin?
35493.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child forbids any disadvantage because of skin colour, origin, language or religion.
35493.m: No child may be disadvantaged because of their skin colour.

35494.q: Do girls and boys have the same children's rights?
35494.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child forbids disadvantage because of sex. Girls and boys have the same rights.
35494.m: Girls and boys have the same children's rights.

35495.q: According to children's rights, what do children with a disability have?
a: A duty to stay at home
35495.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child says that children with a disability get special help so that they can take an active part in life.
35495.m: Children with a disability have a right to special support.

35496.q: A child speaks Portuguese at home. What rights do they have in Switzerland?
a: All of them only with a Swiss passport
35496.e: Children's rights apply to every child, no matter what language they speak or where their family comes from.
35496.m: Every language and origin counts equally.

a: Everyone has the same amount of money
35497.e: Equal opportunities means that every child gets the same chances, for example at school, no matter where they come from.
35497.m: Every child should get fair chances.

35498.q: What is it called when someone is unfairly disadvantaged?
35498.e: Discrimination means that someone is treated worse because of a characteristic such as origin or sex. This is forbidden.

35499.q: What helps children in wheelchairs to join in everywhere?
35499.e: Ramps and lifts make buildings accessible without obstacles. That way children in wheelchairs can take part just like others.
35499.m: Ramps and lifts make places accessible to everyone.

35500.q: May a child be punished because their parents did something wrong?
35500.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child protects children from being disadvantaged or punished because of their parents' actions or opinions.
35500.m: Children must not be punished for their parents' mistakes.

35501.e: Privacy is a person's personal space, which others may not simply intrude into. Children have this right too.
35501.m: Every child has their own protected space.

35502.q: May someone simply read your diary?
a: Yes, if it is lying open
35502.e: A diary is private. The right to privacy protects your personal thoughts and notes.
35502.m: My diary belongs only to me.

35503.q: According to children's rights, what else does the right to privacy protect?
35503.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child protects private life, family, home and correspondence, which includes letters.

35504.q: What should you do before you post a photo of a friend on the internet?
35504.e: Everyone may decide for themselves whether a photo of them is published. That is why you always ask first.
35504.m: Before sharing a photo, always ask first.

35505.q: Which piece of information should you not give away on the internet?
35505.e: Your home address is personal information. Strangers could misuse it, so it stays private.
35505.m: My address stays secret on the internet.

35506.q: What does a good password protect?
35506.e: A password stops strangers getting into your accounts and your data. It protects your privacy on the internet.
35506.m: A good password protects my data.

35507.q: May someone spread lies about you that damage your reputation?
a: Yes, on the internet it is
35507.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child protects children from attacks on their honour and reputation. This also applies on the internet.
35507.m: Nobody may damage my reputation with lies.

35508.q: What do you do before you go into your sister's closed room?
35508.e: By knocking you respect other people's privacy. Brothers and sisters have a right to their own space too.

a: When nobody properly looks after a child
When a child is on holiday
35509.e: With neglect, a child does not get enough care, food or attention. The Convention on the Rights of the Child protects children from this too.
35509.m: Neglecting a child also violates their rights.

35510.q: According to children's rights, who must protect children from violence?
35510.e: Countries must create laws and measures so that children are protected. Parents and other adults also have responsibility.
35510.m: Adults and the state must protect children.

35511.q: What should you do if someone hits you?
35511.e: A person you trust, such as a parent, teacher or school social worker, can help. Nobody has to deal with something like that alone.
35511.m: If you experience violence, get help.

35512.q: Where can mothers and children in Switzerland find protection if they experience violence at home?
35512.e: Women's refuges offer women and their children a safe place if they experience violence at home. The address is secret.
35512.m: A women's refuge is a safe place away from violence.

35513.q: What is also violence, not just hitting?
35513.e: Violence can also happen with words, for example through insults, threats or laughing at someone. This hurts the soul.
35513.m: Nasty words can be violence too.

35514.q: What are children called who have to fight in a war?
35514.e: Child soldiers are forced to fight in wars. The Convention on the Rights of the Child and an additional protocol are meant to protect children from this.
35514.m: Children do not belong in war.

35515.q: Which secret do you not have to keep to yourself?
a: A hiding place in a game
35515.e: Nice secrets bring joy. A secret that frightens you, or where someone hurts you, is one you may always tell.
35515.m: I may always tell bad secrets.

35516.q: What does the sentence “My body belongs to me” mean?
a: I may say no to being touched
35516.e: Every child may decide who is allowed to touch them. If a touch feels uncomfortable, you may say no and tell a person you trust.
35516.m: I may say no if I do not like being touched.

35517.q: What does the Swiss Federal Constitution guarantee children and young people?
35517.e: Article 11 of the Federal Constitution says that children and young people are entitled to special protection of their integrity.
35517.m: In Switzerland, children are entitled to special protection.

35518.q: What does the right to your own opinion mean?
a: Children may say what they think
35518.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child gives children the right to express their opinion freely.
35518.m: Children may say what they think.

35519.q: How should adults treat children's opinions?
35519.e: According to the Convention on the Rights of the Child, a child's opinion must be given due weight. Adults should listen and take it seriously.
35519.m: Children's opinions must be taken seriously.

35520.q: What determines how much a child's opinion counts?
35520.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child says that a child's opinion is taken into account according to their age and maturity.
35520.m: The older a child is, the more their opinion counts.

35521.q: According to children's rights, when should children be heard?
35521.e: Children have the right to be heard in all decisions that affect them, for example in court or by the authorities.
35521.m: When it is about me, I may have my say.

35522.q: The class council is deciding about the school trip. What may you do?
35522.e: Children have the right to have a say in decisions that affect them. In the class council everyone may give their opinion, and then the decision is made together.
35522.m: When it is about me, I may give my opinion.

35523.q: According to children's rights, what may children do together?
35523.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child gives children the right to join together with others and to gather peacefully.

35524.q: According to children's rights, how may children express their opinion?
35524.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child allows opinions to be expressed orally, in writing, in print or through art.
35524.m: I may say, write or draw my opinion.

35525.q: What must you bear in mind when you give your opinion?
35525.e: Freedom of opinion has limits: the rights and reputation of other people must be respected.
35525.m: I give my opinion without insulting others.

35526.q: What does the right to information mean?
35526.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child gives children the right to seek, receive and pass on information.
35526.m: Children may ask questions and find things out.

35527.q: Where in the municipality can children find information and borrow books for free?
35527.e: The library has books, magazines and often computers. Children can usually borrow books there for free.
35527.m: The library is a place full of knowledge.

35528.q: According to children's rights, what should countries promote?
35528.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child requires the production and distribution of children's books to be promoted.
35528.m: Children's books help children understand the world.

35529.q: What should children be protected from in the media?
35529.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child says that children should be protected from information that harms them.
35529.m: Not all content on the internet is good for children.

35530.q: What does the age rating on a film or video game show?
a: The age it is suitable from
35530.e: The age rating shows from what age a film or game is suitable. It helps protect children from harmful content.
35530.m: The age rating helps you choose suitable films and games.

35531.q: According to the Convention on the Rights of the Child, who should know about children's rights?
35531.e: Countries must make children's rights known to children and adults. Only people who know their rights can use them.
35531.m: Everyone should know about children's rights.

35532.q: What should you do if you see something on the internet that frightens you?
a: Send it to all your friends
35532.e: An adult you trust can help you understand what you have seen. You do not have to deal with it alone.
35532.m: If something on the internet frightens me, I talk about it.

35533.q: What are news reports that are deliberately false called?
35533.e: Fake news deliberately spreads things that are untrue. That is why it is important to check information and use good sources.
35533.m: Not everything you read is true.

35534.q: What is the big UN treaty on the rights of children called?
a: Convention on the Rights of the Child
35534.e: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child is a treaty between many countries. It sets out the rights that all children have.
35534.m: The Convention on the Rights of the Child writes down the rights of all children.

35535.q: Who do the UN children's rights apply to?
35535.e: Children's rights apply to every child, no matter where they come from, what language they speak or how their family lives.
35535.m: Children's rights apply to every child in the world.

35536.q: What is an article in a treaty such as the Convention on the Rights of the Child?
35536.e: Treaties and laws are divided into numbered sections called articles. The Convention on the Rights of the Child has 54 articles.
35536.m: The Convention on the Rights of the Child has 54 articles.

35537.q: Who adopted the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child?
35537.e: Representatives of almost every country in the world sit in the UN General Assembly. They adopted the convention together.
35537.m: The UN General Assembly adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child.

35538.q: What should come first in all decisions about children?
a: The best interests of the child
35538.e: Article 3 of the convention says that the best interests of the child must be a primary consideration. So you always ask what is good for the child.
35538.m: In decisions about children, the child's best interests come first.

35539.q: How many countries have accepted the Convention on the Rights of the Child?
a: Almost every country in the world
35539.e: Almost every country in the world has accepted the Convention on the Rights of the Child. No other UN human rights treaty has so many members.
35539.m: Almost every country in the world has accepted children's rights.

35540.q: According to the Convention on the Rights of the Child, how must children who have done something forbidden be treated?
35540.e: The convention requires such children to be treated fairly and with respect for their dignity. In prison they must be kept separate from adults.
35540.m: Even children who have done something forbidden are treated fairly.

35541.q: According to Article 6 of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, what right does every child have?
a: The right to a mobile phone
35541.e: Article 6 says that every child has an inherent right to life. Countries should ensure the child's survival and development.
35541.m: Every child has a right to life.

35542.q: According to the Convention on the Rights of the Child, what else must countries protect children from?
35542.e: The convention requires countries to prevent children from being abducted or sold. Countries also work together on this.
35542.m: Children must be protected from abduction.

35543.q: The Convention on the Rights of the Child was adopted in 1989. How old was it on Children's Rights Day 2025?
35543.e: You work it out: 2025 minus 1989 = 36. So on Children's Rights Day 2025 the convention celebrated its 36th birthday.
35543.m: The Convention on the Rights of the Child is more than 30 years old.

35544.q: What does Children's Rights Day commemorate?
a: The Convention on the Rights of the Child
35544.e: The day was chosen because the UN adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child on that date. So every year it reminds people of children's rights.
35544.m: Children's Rights Day commemorates the Convention on the Rights of the Child.

35545.q: How often is there a Children's Rights Day?
35545.e: Children's Rights Day is celebrated every year on the same date. That way people regularly think about children's rights.
35545.m: Children's Rights Day happens once a year.

35546.q: What do many school classes do on Children's Rights Day?
35546.e: On this day many schools talk about children's rights, draw pictures or hold small events. That way children get to know their rights.
35546.m: On Children's Rights Day, children get to know their rights.

35547.q: Is Children's Rights Day a holiday without school in Switzerland?
a: No, it is a school day
Yes, everyone has the day off
Yes, but only in the morning
35547.e: Children's Rights Day is a day of remembrance, not a public holiday. If it falls on a weekday, children go to school as normal.
35547.m: Children in Switzerland have school on Children's Rights Day.

35548.q: Which colour often lights up buildings on Children's Rights Day as part of UNICEF's campaign?
35548.e: In the #GoBlue campaign, buildings, bridges and towers are lit up in blue on Children's Rights Day. It is a sign of support for children.
35548.m: On Children's Rights Day, many buildings light up blue.

35549.q: Why is Children's Rights Day important?
a: So that everyone knows children's rights
So that there is no school
35549.e: Only people who know their rights can claim them. That is why the day makes children's rights known, among children and adults.
35549.m: If you know your rights, you can stand up for yourself better.

35550.q: Where is Children's Rights Day celebrated?
35550.e: Children's Rights Day is an international day. That is why it is marked in many countries all over the world.
35550.m: Children's Rights Day is marked worldwide.

35551.e: UNICEF is part of the United Nations (UN). It helps children all over the world, for example with food, vaccinations and schools.
35551.m: UNICEF is the children's agency of the United Nations.

35552.q: In which city is UNICEF's headquarters?
35552.e: UNICEF has its headquarters in New York, where the UN also has its headquarters.
35552.m: UNICEF's headquarters is in New York.

35553.q: What colour is the UNICEF logo?
35553.e: The UNICEF logo is light blue, like the colour of the United Nations.

35554.q: Who does the UNICEF logo show?
35554.e: In the logo, an adult holds a child up, with a globe behind them. This shows that UNICEF protects children all over the world.
35554.m: The UNICEF logo shows a mother holding her child up.

35555.q: Where does UNICEF get the money for its work?
35555.e: UNICEF relies on voluntary contributions from countries and on donations from many people. Children can help too, for example with fundraising events.

35556.q: Which famous prize did UNICEF receive in 1965?
35556.e: UNICEF received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1965 for its help for children all over the world.
35556.m: UNICEF has won the Nobel Peace Prize.

35557.q: In which year was UNICEF founded?
35557.e: UNICEF was founded on 11 December 1946, shortly after the Second World War. At that time many children in Europe needed help.
35557.m: UNICEF was founded after the Second World War.

35558.q: In which Swiss city is UNICEF Switzerland and Liechtenstein based?
35558.e: UNICEF's Swiss committee is in Zurich. It is also responsible for Liechtenstein.
35558.m: UNICEF Switzerland and Liechtenstein is based in Zurich.

35559.q: What does UNICEF bring to children in many countries to protect them from diseases?
35559.e: UNICEF makes sure that many children are vaccinated. Vaccinations protect against dangerous diseases such as measles.

35560.q: How much does a call to the number 147 cost?
35560.e: Advice via 147 is free of charge. That way all children and young people can call, even without money.

35561.q: When can you call the number 147?
35561.e: The 147 helpline is available around the clock, 24 hours a day. You can call at night too.
35561.m: The number 147 is available day and night.

35562.e: The Pro Juventute foundation runs the 147 helpline. Experts work there who listen to children and young people.

35563.q: Do you have to give your name when you contact 147?
35563.e: With 147 you can stay anonymous. You do not have to give your name if you do not want to.
35563.m: Nobody has to give their name at 147.

35564.q: Apart from by phone, how else can you reach 147?
35564.e: You can call 147, send a text message or write in the chat. That way every child finds the way that suits them best.
35564.m: You can also reach 147 by text or chat.

35565.q: Which worries may you contact 147 about?
35565.e: At 147 you may talk about anything: quarrels, fear, heartbreak, problems at home or at school. No worry is too small.
35565.m: At 147 you may talk about any worry.

35566.q: Who is the number 147 meant for?
35566.e: The 147 helpline is there especially for children and young people in Switzerland. There are separate services for parents.
35566.m: The number 147 is there for children and young people.

35567.q: Which number do you call in Switzerland if someone is badly injured?
35567.e: 144 is the emergency number for the ambulance. 117 is the police, 118 the fire brigade and 147 is there for children's worries.
35567.m: For injured people, you call the ambulance on 144.

35568.q: What does the name “Pro Juventute” mean in English?
35568.e: “Pro Juventute” is Latin and means “for young people”. The foundation stands up for children and young people.

a: A foundation for children and young people
35569.e: Pro Juventute is a Swiss foundation that has existed since 1912. It supports children, young people and parents, for example with the 147 helpline.
35569.m: Pro Juventute is a foundation for children and young people.

35570.q: In which city does Pro Juventute have its headquarters?
35570.e: The headquarters of the Pro Juventute foundation is in Zurich. But it also has offices in other regions of Switzerland.
35570.m: Pro Juventute has its headquarters in Zurich.

35571.q: What kind of organisation is Pro Juventute?
35571.e: Pro Juventute is a foundation. It does not work for profit but helps children, young people and parents.
35571.m: Pro Juventute is a foundation for children and young people.

35572.q: Which disease did Pro Juventute fight when it was founded in 1912?
35572.e: When it was founded, many young people died of tuberculosis, a lung disease. Pro Juventute collected money to help them.
35572.m: Pro Juventute first helped children with tuberculosis.

35573.q: How has Pro Juventute raised money with the help of the post office for over a hundred years?
a: With stamps that carry a surcharge
With a lottery at the post office counter
35573.e: Pro Juventute stamps have existed since 1913. Anyone who buys them pays a small surcharge, which goes to the foundation.
35573.m: Pro Juventute stamps have existed for over a hundred years.

35574.q: Which number can children in Switzerland call for free if they have worries?
35574.e: On 147, Pro Juventute helps children and young people with their worries, day and night. 117 is the police, 118 the fire brigade and 144 the ambulance.
35574.m: If you have worries, the number 147 helps.

35575.q: What does the ZEWO quality seal show about Pro Juventute?
a: You have to be a member
35575.e: The ZEWO quality seal is given to charities that handle donated money honestly and carefully. Pro Juventute has had this seal since 1942.
35575.m: The ZEWO seal shows that donations are put to good use.

a: Protecting children from danger and violence
35576.e: Child protection means that adults make sure children are safe. Nobody may use violence against a child.
35576.m: Child protection means protecting children from violence and danger.

35577.q: Is a child to blame if they are hit?
35577.e: Violence is never the child's fault. The responsibility always lies with the person who hits.
35577.m: Someone who is hit is never to blame.

35578.q: What should you never send to a stranger on the internet?
35578.e: Photos can be forwarded and misused. That is why you never send pictures of yourself to strangers on the internet.
35578.m: I do not send photos of myself to strangers.

35579.q: Who can you tell at school if someone hurts you?
a: Only the person who hurts you
Only when you are grown up
35579.e: Teachers listen to you and help you. They may, and must, get help if a child is in danger.
35579.m: If someone hurts me, I may tell my teacher.

35580.q: A child often gets nothing to eat at home, and nobody cares. What must adults do?
a: Wait until the child is grown up
35580.e: The child is not safe. Then adults must act and get help, for example from an advice centre.
35580.m: If a child is in danger, adults must act.

35581.q: Which authority in Switzerland helps if a child is not safe at home?
35581.e: KESB stands for the child and adult protection authority. It checks whether a child needs protection and arranges help.
35581.m: The KESB protects children who are not safe at home.

35582.q: What is the Swiss foundation that campaigns against violence against children called?
35582.e: The Child Protection Switzerland foundation campaigns for children to grow up without violence. It informs parents, children and professionals.
35582.m: Child Protection Switzerland fights against violence against children.

35583.q: What should a child do if a stranger on the internet wants to meet up?
35583.e: On the internet you never know for sure who is really writing. That is why a child should immediately show such messages to an adult they trust.
35583.m: If you get strange messages online, get help from adults.

35584.e: Forbidden child labour is work that harms children or keeps them from going to school. Small jobs to help at home are not included.
35584.m: Work that harms children is forbidden.

35585.q: Where are many children who have to work often unable to go?
35585.e: Children who have to work often have no time for school. They work, for example, in fields, factories or markets. Without school it is harder to find a good job later.
35585.m: Child labour takes away children's chance of an education.

35586.q: From what age may young people in Switzerland generally do proper work?
35586.e: The Labour Act generally only allows proper work from the age of 15. For younger people there are only exceptions for light work.
35586.m: In Switzerland you may generally only work from the age of 15.

35587.q: Roughly how many children in the world had to work in 2024?
35587.e: UN experts estimated around 138 million children in child labour in 2024 (2025 report). That is far fewer than before, but still a great many.
35587.m: Millions of children worldwide still have to work.

35588.q: On which day is the World Day Against Child Labour?
35588.e: Since 2002, 12 June has been the World Day Against Child Labour. On this day attention is drawn to the problem.
35588.m: 12 June is the World Day Against Child Labour.

35589.q: Which help at home is allowed for children?
35589.e: Small household chores are not forbidden child labour. They are short, safe and leave enough time for school and play.
35589.m: Small chores at home are allowed.

35590.q: Where did many children in Switzerland also have to work in the past?
35590.e: More than 150 years ago, many children in Switzerland worked in factories, for example in spinning mills. Later this was banned by law.
35590.m: In the past, children in Switzerland worked in factories too.

35591.q: How can you often recognise clothes made with attention to fair working conditions?
a: By the colour of the label
35591.e: Marks such as Fairtrade show that rules for fair work are followed. This includes no children having to do hard work.
35591.m: Fair labels on clothes help against child labour.

35592.q: In which Swiss city is the International Labour Organization, which fights child labour, based?
35592.e: The International Labour Organization (ILO) is part of the UN and is based in Geneva. It campaigns for fair work and against child labour.
35592.m: The International Labour Organization is based in Geneva.

35593.q: What does a children's officer in a municipality do?
35593.e: Children's and youth officers make sure the municipality thinks of children. They are the people to contact about children's issues.
35593.m: Children's officers stand up for children in the municipality.

35594.q: Who does a children's officer ask for ideas for the municipality?
35594.e: Children's and youth officers ask children and young people about their wishes and ideas. That way children can have a say.

35595.q: What might a children's officer campaign for, for example?
35595.e: Children's and youth officers promote places for children, for example playgrounds, youth clubs or skate parks.
35595.m: Children's officers make sure there are good places to play.

35596.q: What is an office called where children can complain if their rights are violated?
35596.e: An ombudsman's office hears complaints and helps to find a fair solution. There are also ombudsman's offices just for children's rights.
35596.m: An ombudsman's office helps with complaints.

35597.q: Which country was the first in the world to have an ombudsman for children?
35597.e: In 1981, Norway was the first country to create an ombudsman for children. Many other countries followed later.
35597.m: Norway had the first ombudsman for children.

35598.q: Who are children's and youth officers there for?
35598.e: As the name says, they deal with the concerns of children and young people. These can contact them directly.
35598.m: Children's and youth officers are there for young people.

35599.q: What is an important quality of a good children's officer?
35599.e: Children's officers must listen carefully to children and take their concerns seriously. Only then can they pass on the children's wishes.
35599.m: Good children's officers take children seriously.

35600.q: Who does the children's officer take the children's wishes to?
35600.e: Children's officers take children's concerns into municipal politics. That way the municipal council can consider them in its decisions.
35600.m: Children's officers take children's wishes into politics.

35601.q: Which organisation awards the “Child-Friendly Municipality” label in Switzerland?
35601.e: The “Child-Friendly Municipality” label is an initiative of UNICEF Switzerland and Liechtenstein. Municipalities can apply for it.

35602.q: Does every Swiss municipality have to take part in the “Child-Friendly Municipality” label?
35602.e: Taking part is voluntary. A municipality has to apply to UNICEF itself if it wants the label.
35602.m: Municipalities apply for the label voluntarily.

35603.q: For how many years is the “Child-Friendly Municipality” label valid?
35603.e: The label is awarded for four years. After that the municipality must show what it has achieved to get it again.
35603.m: The “Child-Friendly Municipality” label is valid for four years.

35604.q: What must children be able to do in a child-friendly municipality?
35604.e: In a child-friendly municipality, children are asked for their opinion. They can have a say in things that affect them.
35604.m: In a child-friendly municipality, children have a say.

35605.q: What does a municipality write on the way to the “Child-Friendly Municipality” label?
35605.e: In an action plan, the municipality sets out what it wants to improve for children. Only then is it checked whether it gets the label.
35605.m: An action plan shows what a municipality wants to do for children.

35606.q: What does a child-friendly municipality often have?
35606.e: Child-friendly municipalities pay attention to safe routes, good playgrounds and meeting places. Children should feel comfortable and safe there.
35606.m: Child-friendly municipalities make sure routes are safe.

35607.q: Which city with the Federal Palace has been recognised as a child-friendly city?
35607.e: The Federal Palace is in Bern. The city has received UNICEF's “Child-Friendly Municipality” label.

35610.q: What does a country do when it ratifies a treaty such as the Convention on the Rights of the Child?
a: It commits itself to keeping it
It leaves the UN with it
35610.e: Ratifying means that a country officially accepts a treaty. After that it must keep to the rules.
35610.m: A country that ratifies a treaty must keep to it.

35611.q: Which right does Switzerland fulfil with its state schools?
a: The right to holidays by the sea
35611.e: In Switzerland there are public state schools for all children. In this way Switzerland fulfils the right to education.
35611.m: State schools fulfil the right to education.

35612.q: From what age may a child in Switzerland decide on their religion themselves?
35612.e: The Civil Code says that from the age of 16 a child decides on their religious faith themselves. Before that, the parents have a say.
35612.m: From 16 you decide on your religion yourself.

35613.q: Who must respect children's rights in Switzerland?
35613.e: The Convention on the Rights of the Child places obligations on the state. But parents, schools and all adults should also respect children's rights.
35613.m: All adults should respect children's rights.

35614.q: Which Swiss code of law sets out the rights and duties of parents and children?
35614.e: The Civil Code (ZGB) governs family life, for example the duties of parents. It applies throughout Switzerland.
35614.m: The Civil Code governs family life.

35615.q: Who must Switzerland report to regularly on how it implements children's rights?
a: The UN Committee on the Rights of the Child
35615.e: Every country that has accepted the convention sends reports to the UN Committee on the Rights of the Child. The committee then makes recommendations.
35615.m: Switzerland reports to the UN on children's rights.

35616.q: According to the law, how must parents in Switzerland bring up their children?
a: Only with the help of the school
35616.e: The Civil Code states explicitly that parents must bring up their children without physical punishment and without other degrading treatment.
35616.m: Children have a right to an upbringing without violence.

35617.q: What does a children's rights poster show?
35617.e: A children's rights poster shows the most important rights of children, often with pictures and short sentences. That makes them easy to understand.
35617.m: A children's rights poster shows the rights of children.

35618.q: Where is a children's rights poster often hung up?
35618.e: Many schools hang the poster in the classroom. That way the children see their rights every day.
35618.m: In the classroom, a poster is a reminder of children's rights.

35619.q: Why does a children's rights poster often have lots of pictures?
a: So that young children can understand it too
35619.e: Pictures help children who cannot read well yet. Children who speak a different language also understand the rights better this way.
35619.m: Pictures make children's rights understandable for everyone.

35620.q: A picture on the poster shows a child with a school bag. Which right is meant?
35620.e: The school bag stands for school. Every child has the right to go to school and learn.
35620.m: The school bag stands for the right to education.

35621.q: A picture on the poster shows children from different countries holding hands. Which right is meant?
35621.e: The children holding hands show that all children are of equal worth. No child may be disadvantaged because of origin, language or appearance.
35621.m: The hands stand for the equal treatment of all children.

35622.q: A picture on the poster shows a child with a speech bubble. Which right is meant?
a: The right to your own opinion
35622.e: The speech bubble shows that a child is saying something. Children have the right to give their opinion, and adults should listen.
35622.m: The speech bubble stands for the right to give your own opinion.

35623.q: A picture on the poster shows a child with a full plate. Which right is meant?
35623.e: The full plate stands for enough healthy food. No child should have to go hungry.
35623.m: The plate stands for the right to food.

35624.q: A picture on the poster shows a child under a roof. Which right is meant?
35624.e: The roof stands for a safe home. Every child should be able to live in a protected place.
35624.m: The roof stands for the right to a safe home.

35625.q: Apart from the teacher, who helps with quarrels and worries at school?
35625.e: School social workers are experts in problems and worries. They work directly in the school.
35625.m: School social work helps with worries at school.

35626.q: How much does a talk with the school social worker cost?
35626.e: School social work is a service provided by the school. Children can go there for free.

35627.q: May the school social worker pass on everything a child says?
a: No, she has a duty of confidentiality
35627.e: School social workers have a duty of confidentiality. Only if a child is in danger do they get help, and they tell the child beforehand.
35627.m: What you tell the school social worker stays confidential.

35628.q: With which problem can you go to the school social worker?
35628.e: Bullying is a serious problem that you do not have to solve alone. The school social worker helps to make it stop.
35628.m: School social work helps with bullying.

35629.q: Who may go to the school social worker?
35629.e: School social work is there for all children. You do not need a special reason or permission.
35629.m: Every schoolchild may go to the school social worker.

35630.q: Where does the school social worker usually work?
35630.e: The school social worker usually has an office right in the school building. That makes them easy for children to find.
35630.m: School social work is right in the school building.

35631.q: How does the school social worker help with quarrels in the class?
a: They help with talking and making up
35631.e: The school social worker helps children talk to each other and find a solution. They give no marks and no punishments.
35631.m: School social work helps to settle quarrels peacefully.

35632.q: Apart from children, who else can ask the school social worker for advice?
35632.e: Parents and teachers can also contact the school social worker. Together they then look for a good solution for the child.
35632.m: Parents and teachers may also ask the school social worker.

35633.q: What is one of the tasks of school social work?
35633.e: School social workers advise children when they have worries. Teachers still do the teaching.
35633.m: School social work advises children who have worries.

35634.q: Who takes part in the class council?
a: All the children in the class
