35634.e: In the class council the whole class sits together. Every child may have a say and help decide.
35634.m: All the children in the class belong to the class council.

35635.q: How does a class often sit for the class council?
a: One behind the other on the floor
Each child alone in the corridor
35635.e: In a circle all the children can see each other well. That makes it easier to talk to one another.
35635.m: In a circle, everyone in the class council can see each other.

35636.q: Who often leads the class council?
35636.e: Often a child leads the class council. This job rotates so that every child gets a chance to practise it.
35636.m: In the class council, children may take the lead too.

35637.q: How often does a class council take place in many classes?
a: Only on the last day of school
35637.e: In many classes the class council takes place regularly, often once a week. That way problems can be discussed early.

35638.q: What does a class talk about in the class council?
35638.e: The class council is about living together as a class. People talk about quarrels, wishes and ideas such as a trip.
35638.m: In the class council, children discuss things that matter to them all.

35639.q: How can a class decide in the class council?
35639.e: In the class council, the children often vote on a proposal. Then what most of them want applies.
35639.m: In a vote, every vote counts the same.

35640.q: What does the class council look for when there is a quarrel?
a: Someone to blame and laugh at
35640.e: In the class council, quarrels should be settled fairly. Everyone involved may tell their side, and then a solution is found together.
35640.m: The class council helps to settle quarrels fairly.

35641.q: What do you practise especially well in the class council?
35641.e: In the class council children learn to give their opinion and to listen to others. That is important for living together.
35641.m: In the class council you learn to talk to each other.

35642.q: Who usually sits on the school council?
35642.e: Each class sends one or two children to the school council. These children represent their class.
35642.m: On the school council, children represent their classes.

35643.q: How does a child get onto the school council?
35643.e: The children in a class elect who should represent them on the school council. That makes the choice fair.
35643.m: You are elected to the school council by your class.

35644.q: What does the school council talk about?
35644.e: The school council discusses topics that affect all the children in the school. That might be the playground or a school party, for example.
35644.m: The school council deals with matters concerning the whole school.

35645.q: What does a child on the school council do after the meeting?
a: They tell the class about it
35645.e: The representatives bring the information from the school council back to their class. That way everyone knows what was discussed.
35645.m: Anyone on the school council informs their class afterwards.

35646.q: Which adult often supports the school council?
35646.e: Usually a teacher helps the school council. They support the children, but the children prepare the decisions.
35646.m: A teacher supports the school council.

35647.q: What might a school council plan, for example?
a: An election of the Federal Council
35647.e: A school council can plan events for the school, for example a school party or a sports day.
35647.m: The school council can plan events for the school.

35648.q: What does a child from the class bring to the school council?
35648.e: The child on the school council speaks for their class. That is why they bring the class's ideas and wishes.
35648.m: The classes' wishes are put forward on the school council.

35649.q: What is a meeting called where children from a school debate as in a parliament?
35649.e: In a school parliament, elected children from many classes meet. They debate and vote like adults in parliament.
35649.m: In the school parliament, children debate as in a real parliament.

35650.q: Who is sent to a school parliament?
a: All the parents at the school
35650.e: Each class elects children to represent it in the school parliament. These children are called delegates.
35650.m: Children are elected to the school parliament by their classes.

35651.q: How do you often show in the school parliament what you are voting for?
35651.e: When voting, the children often raise their hands. Then people count how many are for or against.
35651.m: You can vote by raising your hand.

35652.q: In the school parliament, what applies if most people vote for a proposal?
35652.e: If the majority vote Yes, a proposal is accepted. That is how decisions are made in a democracy.
35652.m: The majority decides on a proposal.

35653.q: What is a motion in the school parliament?
35653.e: A motion is a proposal that the meeting is to vote on. For example: “We would like a football goal in the playground.”
35653.m: A motion is a proposal that is voted on.

35654.q: Who leads the meeting in a school parliament?
a: The youngest child in the school
35654.e: The school parliament often elects a presidency. The president leads the meeting and gives people the floor.
35654.m: A presidency leads the meeting in the school parliament.

35655.q: What do you learn about Switzerland in a school parliament?
35655.e: In the school parliament, children elect and vote like adults. That way they learn how democracy works.
35655.m: In the school parliament, children practise democracy.

35656.q: What does a child do who wants to speak in the school parliament?
35656.e: In the school parliament you put your hand up before you speak. The chair then gives you the floor so that everyone gets a turn.
35656.m: In parliament you put your hand up before you speak.

35657.q: Who may take part in a children's parliament?
35657.e: A children's parliament is a parliament for children. There, children put forward their ideas for their town or municipality.
35657.m: In the children's parliament, children have a say about their municipality.

35658.q: What do children in a children's parliament often campaign for?
35658.e: Children's parliaments exist in towns and municipalities, for example. The children make suggestions for making where they live more child-friendly.
35658.m: Children's parliaments make suggestions for where they live.

35659.q: What is a member of a children's parliament called?
35659.e: Someone who sits in a children's parliament is called a child parliamentarian.
35659.m: Child parliamentarians sit in the children's parliament.

35660.q: Who does a children's parliament often pass its ideas on to?
35660.e: A children's parliament writes down its wishes and passes them on to the authorities. The adults then check what they can put into practice.
35660.m: The children's parliament takes ideas to the authorities.

35661.q: Which topic suits a children's parliament well?
35661.e: Children know their route to school very well. That is why they can show in the children's parliament where it is dangerous.
35661.m: Children know well where their route to school is dangerous.

35662.q: How do you become a member of many children's parliaments?
a: You are elected or you sign up
35662.e: In many children's parliaments, school classes elect the members. Sometimes children can also simply sign up.
35662.m: You get into the children's parliament by election or by signing up.

a: A meeting where children have a say
35663.e: In a children's parliament, children debate topics that affect them. In doing so they learn how politics works.
35663.m: A children's parliament gives children a voice.

35664.q: What does a child practise when they give a speech in the children's parliament?
35664.e: Anyone presenting an idea in the children's parliament speaks in front of many people. That takes courage and is good practice.
35664.m: In the children's parliament you practise speaking in front of others.

35665.q: In which city does the Federal Youth Session take place?
35665.e: The Youth Session takes place in the federal city of Bern. That is also where the Swiss parliament works.
35665.m: The Federal Youth Session takes place in Bern.

35666.q: In which building do the young people debate at the Youth Session?
35666.e: The big debate of the Youth Session takes place in the Federal Palace. That is where the Swiss parliament usually meets.
35666.m: The Youth Session debates in the Federal Palace.

35667.q: About how many young people take part in the Youth Session?
35667.e: Every year around 200 young people from all over Switzerland take part in the Federal Youth Session.
35667.m: Around 200 young people come to the Youth Session.

35668.q: How old are the young people at the Youth Session?
35668.e: Young people aged 14 to 21 may take part in the Federal Youth Session.
35668.m: The Youth Session is for young people aged 14 to 21.

35669.q: In which season does the Youth Session take place?
35669.e: The Federal Youth Session takes place every year in autumn. It lasts several days.
35669.m: The Youth Session takes place every autumn.

35670.q: Which area do the young people at the Youth Session come from?
35670.e: The Youth Session is federal. That is why the young people come from all parts of Switzerland.
35670.m: At the Youth Session, young people from all over Switzerland meet.

35671.q: What does the President of the National Council receive from the Youth Session?
35671.e: The young people adopt demands, known as petitions. These are handed to the head of the National Council and passed on to committees.
35671.m: The Youth Session's demands go to parliament.

35672.q: In which language may the young people speak at the Youth Session?
35672.e: At the Youth Session, young people from all language regions meet. They may speak in their national language, and it is translated.
35672.m: The Youth Session is multilingual, like Switzerland.

35673.q: Who held discussions at the Children's Conference in eastern Switzerland?
35673.e: At the Children's Conference, children from several cantons met. They talked about their own concerns.
35673.m: At a children's conference, children talk about their concerns.

35674.q: In which place in the Appenzell region did the Children's Conference take place?
35674.e: The Children's Conference took place in Trogen. Trogen is in the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden.
35674.m: The Children's Conference took place in Trogen.

35675.q: Which rights were often the subject of the Children's Conference?
35675.e: The Children's Conference was about children's rights. The children thought about how these rights could be better put into practice in Switzerland.

35676.q: Who discusses their own concerns at a children's conference?
35676.e: At a children's conference, children talk about topics that affect them, for example their rights. Adults listen and take the ideas away with them.
35676.m: At a children's conference, children have a say.

35677.q: What did the children work out at the Children's Conference?
35677.e: The children talked about their topics in workshops. Then they wrote down demands and passed them on to adults in politics.
35677.m: At the Children's Conference, children wrote demands for politicians.

35678.q: Who chose the workshop topics at the Children's Conference?
35678.e: At the Children's Conference, the children were allowed to choose the topics of their workshops themselves. So it was about what mattered to them.
35678.m: At the Children's Conference, children chose their topics themselves.

35679.q: Roughly how long did the Children's Conference in Trogen last?
35679.e: The Children's Conference lasted a few days, five most recently. During this time the children stayed at the conference venue.
35679.m: The Children's Conference lasted a few days.

35680.q: What do you put into a suggestion box?
35680.e: You put notes with ideas or wishes into a suggestion box. Later the notes are read and discussed.
35680.m: Notes with ideas go into the suggestion box.

35681.q: What is a suggestion box in the school good for?
35681.e: With a suggestion box, every child can write down their idea. That way quiet children are heard too.
35681.m: With the suggestion box, every child can put forward an idea.

35682.q: What is handy about not writing your name on a note for the suggestion box?
35682.e: You can put in a note without a name. Then you might feel braver about raising a problem.
35682.m: You may put in a suggestion without your name.

35683.q: When is the suggestion box often opened in the class?
35683.e: Many classes open the suggestion box in the class council. Then the notes are read out and discussed.
35683.m: The notes from the box are discussed in the class council.

35684.q: What else can you call a suggestion box?
35684.e: A suggestion box is like a small postbox. Instead of letters, ideas and wishes go into it.
35684.m: A suggestion box is a postbox for ideas.

35685.q: What should a good note for the suggestion box contain?
a: Just a drawing with no meaning
35685.e: A good suggestion is worded clearly and kindly. Then everyone understands what is wanted.
35685.m: A good suggestion is clear and kind.

35686.q: At best, what happens to a good suggestion from the box?
35686.e: Good suggestions are discussed and, if possible, put into practice. That way the school changes with the children's ideas.

35687.q: Who knows well what is fun in a playground?
35687.e: Children use the playground themselves. That is why they know best which play equipment they like.
35687.m: Children are the experts on their playground.

35688.q: How can children have a say in a new playground?
a: They pay for all the equipment
35688.e: In many projects, children may make drawings or models. Planners look at the wishes and build them in if possible.
35688.m: Children can draw their wishes for the playground.

35689.q: Who often decides in the end about a new municipal playground?
35689.e: The municipality owns and pays for many playgrounds. It decides in the end, but may include the children's ideas.
35689.m: The municipality decides about its playgrounds.

35690.q: Where can children often hand in their playground wishes?
a: In a survey by the municipality
35690.e: Some municipalities carry out a survey among children before building. That way they find out what the children would like.
35690.m: With a survey, the municipality finds out children's wishes.

35691.q: Children walk round the site for a new playground with adults. What do the children show?
a: What they like and what is missing
35691.e: On a walk like this, the children show on the spot what they like and what is missing. The adults write down the ideas.
35691.m: On a walk round the site, children show their ideas on the spot.

35692.q: Which piece of play equipment might children wish for, for example?
35692.e: A slide is a typical piece of play equipment. In the planning, children may say which equipment they would like.
35692.m: A slide is a popular piece of play equipment.

35693.q: Why should children have a say in planning a playground?
a: Because it is being built for them
35693.e: A playground is meant for children. If they have a say, it suits their wishes better.
35693.m: Whoever uses a place should be allowed to have a say.

35694.q: What can children build to plan a playground?
35694.e: Children can build a model out of cardboard, clay or wood. That shows clearly what the playground could look like.
35694.m: You can plan a playground with a model.

35695.q: Who sits on a youth council?
35695.e: A youth council is made up of young people from a municipality, a town or a canton. They represent the concerns of young people.
35695.m: On the youth council, young people represent their concerns.

35696.q: What does a youth council do in a municipality?
a: It puts forward young people's ideas
35696.e: The youth council collects young people's wishes. It passes them on to the municipality or carries out its own projects.
35696.m: A youth council brings young people's voice into the municipality.

35697.q: Which project might a youth council plan?
35697.e: A youth council might campaign for a meeting place for young people, for example. The municipality plans large buildings.
35697.m: A youth council can campaign for a youth club.

35698.q: How do you often get onto a youth council?
35698.e: You are elected to some youth councils. For others you can volunteer or apply.
35698.m: You get onto a youth council by election or application.

35699.q: Who does a youth council often work with?
35699.e: A youth council talks to the municipality's authorities. That way young people's ideas can be put into practice.
35699.m: The youth council works with the municipality.

35700.q: What is one difference between a youth council and a municipal council?
a: Young people sit on the youth council
Only teachers sit on the youth council
Only parents sit on the youth council
Only pensioners sit on the youth council
35700.e: Elected adults sit on the municipal council. Young people sit on the youth council and bring in their point of view.
35700.m: On the youth council, it is young people's turn.

35701.q: What do young people learn on a youth council?
35701.e: On the youth council, young people attend meetings, plan projects and talk to the authorities. That way they get to know politics.
35701.m: On the youth council, you get to know politics.

35702.q: Who sits on a children's municipal council?
35702.e: A children's municipal council is a group of children from a municipality. They talk about topics that affect children.
35702.m: Children from the municipality sit on the children's municipal council.

35703.q: What is a children's municipal council modelled on?
35703.e: The children's municipal council works in a similar way to the adults' municipal council. Only children sit on it.
35703.m: The children's municipal council is like a municipal council for children.

35704.q: Who does a children's municipal council sometimes meet?
35704.e: A children's municipal council can present its ideas to the adults of the municipality. For this it often meets the mayor.
35704.m: The children's municipal council presents its ideas to the municipality.

35705.q: What idea might a children's municipal council have?
35705.e: Children often get around by bike. That is why they would like safe cycle paths.
35705.m: A children's municipal council stands up for children in the municipality.

35706.q: Why are there children's municipal councils?
a: So that children can have a say
So that children do not go to school
35706.e: Children cannot vote in municipal elections yet. On the children's municipal council they can still put forward their opinion.
35706.m: Children should have a say in things that affect them.

35707.q: What does a children's municipal council sometimes get for its projects?
35707.e: Some children's municipal councils get a little money from the municipality. With it they can carry out their own small projects.
35707.m: With a small budget you can carry out your own projects.

35708.q: Roughly how often does a children's municipal council meet?
35708.e: A children's municipal council meets several times a year. That is where it plans its projects.
35708.m: The children's municipal council meets regularly.

35709.q: How does a child often get onto the children's municipal council?
35709.e: Often the children in the schools elect who goes onto the children's municipal council. That way the group is made up fairly.
35709.m: Children elect their representatives to the children's municipal council.

35710.q: What helps everyone in a large group to speak in turn?
35710.e: A speakers' list has the names of the children who have put their hands up. They then get their turn one after the other.
35710.m: A speakers' list makes sure everyone gets a turn.

35711.q: Which document gives children the right to be heard?
a: The Convention on the Rights of the Child
35711.e: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child says that children may give their opinion on things that affect them. Switzerland has accepted this convention.
35711.m: Children have the right to be heard.

35712.q: How do you give your opinion in a friendly way?
35712.e: If you start with “I think”, you are talking about yourself. That way you do not attack anyone.
35712.m: With an I-sentence you give your opinion in a friendly way.

35713.q: What do you do when someone else is talking?
35713.e: Good listening means letting the other person finish. That way everyone feels taken seriously.

35714.q: What is fine if two children have different opinions?
a: One of them has to leave
35714.e: People often have different opinions. In a democracy you talk about them and find a way forward.

35715.q: Where do you look when someone is talking to you?
35715.e: Looking at the person speaking shows that you are listening. That is polite.
35715.m: When listening, you look at the person speaking.

35716.q: What does a good listener do if they did not understand something?
35716.e: If you did not understand something, you may ask politely. That way there are fewer misunderstandings.

35717.q: What should you avoid when you criticise a different opinion?
35717.e: You may criticise an opinion, but not insult the person. That way the conversation stays fair.
35717.m: You criticise an idea, not the person.

35718.q: What does a talking stick show in a discussion circle?
35718.e: Only the person holding the talking stick may speak. The others listen until the stick is passed on.
35718.m: Whoever has the talking stick may speak.

35719.q: Why do you give reasons for your opinion?
35719.e: A reason makes clear why you think something. Then the others can think about it better.
35719.m: An opinion with a reason is easier to understand.

35720.q: What do you write in the minutes?
a: What was discussed at a meeting
35720.e: The minutes record what was said and decided at a meeting. That way you can read it again later.
35720.m: The minutes record what was discussed.

35721.q: What is the person who writes the minutes called?
35721.e: The person who writes the minutes is called the minute-taker. This person takes notes during the meeting.

35722.q: What do you need minutes for?
a: So that decisions are not forgotten
So that it does not rain
35722.e: With minutes you do not forget what was decided. You can read them again at the next meeting.

35723.q: What goes at the top of the minutes?
35723.e: Minutes begin with the date and usually the place too. That way you know when the meeting was.

35724.q: Whose names do you write in the minutes?
a: The names of all the pets
The names of the Federal Councillors
35724.e: The minutes say who was at the meeting. Sometimes they also say who was absent.
35724.m: The minutes say who was there.

35725.q: What is especially important to record in the minutes?
35725.e: The decisions are the most important part of the minutes. They show what was agreed.
35725.m: The minutes mainly contain the decisions.

35726.q: What is the best way to write minutes?
a: As long and confusing as possible
35726.e: Good minutes are short and clear. You write down the most important things, not every word.
35726.m: Good minutes are short and clear.

35727.q: What often comes at the end of the minutes?
35727.e: At the end it often says who wrote the minutes. That way you know whom to ask.
35727.m: The writer's name often comes at the end of the minutes.

35728.q: In which year did the first Federal Youth Session take place?
35728.e: The first Youth Session took place in 1991 for the 700th anniversary of the Swiss Confederation. It has been held every year since 1993.
35728.m: The first Youth Session was in 1991.

35729.q: About how many days does the Federal Youth Session last?
35729.e: The Youth Session lasts four days. During this time the young people work in groups and debate in the Federal Palace.
35729.m: The Youth Session lasts a few days.

35730.q: Before a school council meeting, what do you write on a list?
a: What you want to talk about
What there is for afternoon snack
What the weather will be like
35730.e: Before the meeting you write down what you want to talk about. This list is called the agenda. That way everyone knows what is coming up.
35730.m: A list shows what will be discussed at the meeting.

35731.q: What was the children's village called where the Children's Conference took place?
35731.e: Until 2021, the Children's Conference took place in the Pestalozzi Children's Village. It is named after the educator Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi.
35731.m: The Pestalozzi Children's Village is named after a famous educator.

35732.q: Where is the best place to hang or put a suggestion box?
a: Somewhere easy to see in the school
35732.e: A suggestion box should be easy to find. Then lots of children use it.
35732.m: A suggestion box goes where everyone can see it.

35733.q: Who is a youth council there for?
a: The young people of a place
35733.e: A youth council represents the young people of a place. It makes sure their concerns are heard.
35733.m: The youth council is there for young people.

35734.q: How many years does compulsory schooling last in most Swiss cantons?
35734.e: In most cantons, compulsory schooling includes 2 years of kindergarten and 9 years of school. Together that makes 11 years.
35734.m: Compulsory schooling lasts 11 years in most cantons.

35735.q: What does school start with for most children in Switzerland?
35735.e: In most cantons, kindergarten is already part of school. Primary school follows after that.

35736.q: At what age do children start kindergarten in most cantons?
35736.e: In most cantons, kindergarten starts when a child is about 4 years old. A cut-off date in summer decides.
35736.m: For many children, kindergarten starts at about four.

35737.q: How much do lessons at a state school in Switzerland cost?
35737.e: The Federal Constitution says that basic education at state schools is free of charge. It is paid for with tax money.
35737.m: Families pay no school fees for lessons at state schools.

35738.q: Who must make sure that a child goes to school?
35738.e: Parents are responsible for making sure their child attends school. They also excuse the child when they are ill.
35738.m: Parents make sure their child goes to school regularly.

35739.q: Who mainly decides how state schools are organised in Switzerland?
35739.e: In Switzerland, state schools are a matter for the cantons. That is why there are small differences between the cantons.
35739.m: The cantons are responsible for state schools.

35740.q: What must parents do if their child is ill and cannot go to school?
35740.e: If you are ill you may stay at home. But the parents tell the school that the child is absent.
35740.m: When a child is ill, the parents excuse them at school.

35741.q: What is the curriculum used by the German-speaking cantons for state schools called?
35741.e: The 21 German-speaking and multilingual cantons have a shared curriculum. It is called Lehrplan 21 (Curriculum 21).
35741.m: Lehrplan 21 applies in the German-speaking Swiss cantons.

35742.e: Taxes are money that people and companies pay to the state. Shared tasks are paid for with it.
35742.m: With taxes, we all pay together for shared tasks.

35743.q: Which tax do you pay even as a child when you buy something in a shop?
35743.e: Value added tax (VAT) is already included in the price of many goods. That is why everyone who shops pays it, even a child.
35743.m: When you shop, the VAT is already included in the price.

35744.q: What is the standard rate of VAT in Switzerland (as of 2026)?
35744.e: Since 2024, the standard rate of VAT has been 8.1 per cent. A lower rate applies to food.
35744.m: The standard rate of VAT is 8.1 per cent.

35745.q: What is the reduced VAT rate, for example for bread and books (as of 2026)?
35745.e: A reduced rate applies to important things such as food and books. Since 2024 it has been 2.6 per cent.
35745.m: A lower VAT rate applies to food and books.

35746.q: Which tax do people pay who keep a dog?
35746.e: Anyone who has a dog in Switzerland pays a dog tax. It usually goes to the municipality.
35746.m: For a dog you pay a dog tax to the municipality.

35747.q: What is paid for with tax money, for example?
35747.e: With tax money the state pays for tasks that serve everyone. These include the police, schools and roads.
35747.m: Taxes pay for things that are useful to everyone.

35748.q: Which tax is included in the price of petrol when you fill up?
35748.e: The Confederation levies mineral oil tax on petrol and diesel. Part of it is used for roads.
35748.m: The price of petrol includes mineral oil tax.

35749.q: What do you call someone who deliberately pays too little tax?
35749.e: Anyone who deliberately hides income or wealth is evading tax. This is forbidden and is punished.
35749.m: Tax evasion is forbidden and is punished.

35750.q: For whom is military service voluntary in Switzerland?
35750.e: Swiss men are obliged to do service. Swiss women may do military service voluntarily.
35750.m: In Switzerland, women can do military service voluntarily.

35751.q: What is the money called that soldiers receive to replace their wages during service?
35751.e: Anyone doing service cannot work and earns no wages. That is why they get loss of earnings compensation, known as EO.
35751.m: During service you get loss of earnings compensation instead of wages.

35752.q: How long does recruit school usually last (as of 2026)?
35752.e: Normal recruit school lasts 18 weeks. For special troops it can last longer.

35753.q: What do you call a person who is currently at recruit school?
35753.e: At recruit school the young people are called recruits. After that they are soldiers.
35753.m: Someone at recruit school is a recruit.

35754.q: When does the orientation day take place for young Swiss men?
35754.e: The orientation day takes place in the year in which you turn 18. There the young people find out what options there are.
35754.m: On the orientation day, young people learn all about service.

35755.q: Where is it checked whether someone is suitable for the army?
35755.e: At recruitment you are examined and tested. Afterwards you know whether and where you will do service.
35755.m: At recruitment it is decided where someone will do service.

35756.q: What does a man who is obliged to serve but does not do service pay?
35756.e: Anyone who is obliged to serve but does no service pays the military service exemption tax. It is 3 per cent of income.
35756.m: Anyone who does no service pays a compensatory tax.

35757.q: What do Swiss soldiers keep at home between periods of service?
a: Nothing at all, everything stays in the barracks
35757.e: In the militia army, soldiers take their personal equipment home with them. This includes, for example, uniform, helmet and rucksack.
35757.m: Swiss soldiers keep their personal equipment at home.

35758.q: Where do recruits usually live during recruit school?
a: In a tent by a lake
35758.e: During recruit school, recruits usually sleep in barracks during the week. At weekends they are often allowed home.
35758.m: Recruits usually live in barracks during the week.

35760.q: Where can you do civilian service, for example?
35760.e: People doing civilian service work, for example, in hospitals, old people's homes, schools or nature conservation. They help the community there.
35760.m: Civilian service workers help in homes, hospitals, schools and nature.

35761.q: How long does civilian service last compared with military service?
a: One and a half times as long
35761.e: Civilian service lasts one and a half times as long as military service. This shows that you are serious about it.
35761.m: Civilian service lasts longer than military service.

35762.q: Since which year has civilian service existed in Switzerland?
35762.e: The Civilian Service Act came into force in 1996. Before that, people who refused service were usually punished.
35762.m: Civilian service has existed in Switzerland since 1996.

35763.q: When may you do civilian service instead of military service?
a: When it goes against your conscience
When you do not feel like it
35763.e: Civilian service is for people who cannot reconcile military service with their conscience. Personal convenience is not enough.
35763.m: Civilian service is for people who cannot do military service for reasons of conscience.

35764.q: What do people doing civilian service carry at work?
35764.e: Civilian service is service without a weapon. The people doing it work for society, for example in care.
35764.m: In civilian service you carry no weapon.

35765.q: Who does someone doing civilian service help in nature conservation, for example?
35765.e: In nature conservation, civilian service workers look after meadows, hedges and footpaths, for example. That way they help plants and animals.
35765.m: Civilian service workers can do good in nature too.

35766.q: What is the place called where someone doing civilian service works?
35766.e: A civilian service worker works at a recognised placement organisation. That might be a home, a hospital or a school.
35766.m: Civilian service workers work at a recognised placement organisation.

35767.q: What is the fire service obligation?
a: The duty to help in the fire brigade
The duty to buy a fire extinguisher
The duty to pay for a fire engine
The duty to attend the fire brigade party every year
35767.e: In many cantons, adults must serve in the fire brigade or pay instead. This is called the fire service obligation.
35767.m: Many municipalities have a fire service obligation for adults.

35768.q: What do you often pay if you do not do fire brigade service?
35768.e: In many municipalities, anyone who is obliged to serve in the fire brigade but does not pays a compensatory tax. The money supports the fire brigade.
35768.m: Anyone who does not help in the fire brigade often pays a compensatory tax.

35769.q: Who must do fire brigade service or pay in many municipalities today?
35769.e: In the past, the fire service obligation often applied only to men. Today in many municipalities it applies to women and men.
35769.m: The fire service obligation now applies to women and men.

35770.q: Who regulates the fire service obligation in Switzerland?
35770.e: The fire brigade is a matter for the cantons and municipalities. That is why the rules are not the same everywhere.
35770.m: Cantons and municipalities regulate the fire brigade.

35771.q: Why is there a fire service obligation?
a: So that there are enough helpers
So that the army needs fewer soldiers
So that the police do not have to report fires
So that houses do not need smoke alarms
35771.e: Most fire brigades are made up of volunteers and people obliged to serve. That way every municipality has enough people for emergencies.
35771.m: The fire service obligation makes sure enough people can help.

35772.q: What do firefighters do at a fire brigade drill?
a: They practise putting out fires and rescuing
They inspect every flat in the village
35772.e: Firefighters meet regularly for drills. There they learn how to put out fires and rescue people.

35773.q: Where can children and young people already take part in the fire brigade?
35773.e: Many fire brigades have a youth fire brigade. There young people learn in a playful way what the fire brigade does.
35773.m: In the youth fire brigade, young people get to know the work of the fire brigade.

35774.q: What do firefighters in many municipalities get for drills and call-outs?
35774.e: Many municipalities pay their firefighters a small payment. It is compensation for the time they give.
35774.m: Firefighters often get a small payment for their service.

35775.q: Which right does the duty to go to school belong to?
a: The right to a mobile phone
35775.e: Every child has the right to learn. To make this work, there is also the duty to go to school.
35775.m: The right to education comes with the duty to go to school.

35776.q: I may give my opinion. Which duty goes with it?
35776.e: Everyone may give their opinion. But you must also respect other people's opinions.
35776.m: If you give your opinion, you also listen to others with respect.

35777.q: What duty do all people in Switzerland have towards the laws?
35777.e: Laws apply to everyone in the country. That is why everyone must obey them, including adults and the authorities.

35778.q: What is it called when you are an adult in the eyes of the law at 18?
35778.e: In Switzerland you come of age at 18. Then you have more rights, but also more duties.
35778.m: In Switzerland you come of age at 18.

35779.q: Why do rights and duties belong together?
a: So that there are no rules
35779.e: If everyone only had rights, nobody would look after others. Duties make sure everyone's rights are protected.
35779.m: Rights and duties together make good living together possible.

35780.q: What right does a child have in decisions that affect them?
35780.e: The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child says that children may give their opinion when it concerns them. Adults should take this opinion seriously.
35780.m: Children have the right to give their opinion when it concerns them.

35781.q: What is the money penalty called when someone breaks a rule, for example parks in the wrong place?
35781.e: Anyone who breaks a rule often has to pay a fine. That shows that duties are meant seriously.
35781.m: Anyone who breaks a rule sometimes has to pay a fine.

35782.q: What is insurance, explained very simply?
a: Many pay in, and whoever has bad luck gets help
A piggy bank just for me
35782.e: With insurance, many people regularly pay an amount. If someone suffers damage, they get money from this shared pot.
35782.m: With insurance, many people help together when someone has bad luck.

35783.q: What is the amount you pay regularly for insurance called?
35783.e: For insurance you pay a premium. This is an amount per month or per year, for example.
35783.m: For insurance you pay a premium.

35784.q: Which insurance must every person in Switzerland have?
35784.e: Basic health insurance is compulsory in Switzerland. This also applies to children and babies.
35784.m: In Switzerland every person needs health insurance.

35785.q: Since which year has health insurance been compulsory for everyone in Switzerland?
35785.e: The Health Insurance Act has applied since 1996. Since then every person in Switzerland must have basic insurance.
35785.m: Health insurance has been compulsory in Switzerland since 1996.

35786.q: Which insurance pays if I accidentally break my neighbour's window?
35786.e: Liability insurance pays for damage you accidentally cause to others. Many families have this kind of insurance.
35786.m: Liability insurance pays for damage I cause to others.

35787.q: Which insurance must every car in Switzerland have?
35787.e: Motor vehicle liability insurance is compulsory for every car. It pays for damage you cause to others with the car.

35788.q: Which insurance helps if my home is burgled?
35788.e: Household contents insurance pays for things in the flat that are stolen or damaged. These include furniture, clothes and appliances.
35788.m: Household contents insurance protects the things in your home.

35789.q: Which insurance pays the costs if someone is injured at work?
35789.e: Anyone who is employed is insured against accidents. Accident insurance then pays for the doctor and hospital, for example.

35790.q: What do you show at the doctor's surgery so that your health insurer is known?
35790.e: The insurance card shows which health insurer you are insured with. That is why you take it to the doctor's.
35790.m: You take your health insurance card to the doctor's.

35791.q: Who mainly gets money from the AHV?
35791.e: When people no longer work because they are old, they get a pension from the AHV. That way they have money to live on in old age too.
35791.m: The AHV pays older people a pension.

35792.q: What is the money called that you get from the AHV every month in old age?
35792.e: The AHV pays a pension every month. It is money for people who have retired.
35792.m: The money from the AHV in old age is called a pension.

35793.q: Apart from old people, who else gets money from the AHV?
35793.e: Survivors are widows, widowers and orphans. If a parent dies, the AHV helps the family with a pension.
35793.m: The AHV also helps families when a parent has died.

35794.q: Where does the AHV's money mainly come from?
35794.e: Anyone who works pays part of their wages into the AHV. The company pays the same amount on top, and the Confederation helps too.
35794.m: Today's workers help pay today's pensions.

35795.q: At what age do men in Switzerland normally get the AHV pension (as of 2026)?
35795.e: The reference age for the AHV pension is 65 for men. For women it is also rising step by step to 65.
35795.m: The reference age for the AHV is 65.

35796.q: What else is the AHV called in the Swiss pension system?
35796.e: Switzerland's pension system has three pillars. The AHV is the first pillar.
35796.m: The AHV is the first pillar of the pension system.

35797.q: How many AHV pensions per year did the people decide on in 2024?
35797.e: In March 2024 the people said Yes to a 13th AHV pension. It will be paid from December 2026.
35797.m: In 2024 the people decided on a 13th AHV pension.

35798.e: Fundamental rights are the most important rights that every person has. They are in the Federal Constitution and protect everyone.
35798.m: Fundamental rights protect all people in Switzerland.

35799.q: Which fundamental right comes right at the start of the fundamental rights in the Federal Constitution?
35799.e: Article 7 says that human dignity must be respected and protected. The fundamental rights begin with this.
35799.m: Every person's dignity must be respected.

35800.q: What does equality before the law mean?
a: Everyone is equal before the law
Everyone has the same amount of money
35800.e: The Federal Constitution says that all people are equal before the law. Nobody may be disadvantaged because of origin, sex or religion.
35800.m: All people are equal before the law.

35801.q: What does the Federal Constitution say about children?
a: They may never give their opinion
35801.e: Article 11 of the Federal Constitution says that children and young people are specially protected and supported. They should be able to develop well.
35801.m: Children have a right to special protection and support.

35802.q: What does freedom of religion allow?
35802.e: Every person may decide for themselves whether and what they believe. Nobody may be forced into a religion.
35802.m: Every person may choose their religion freely.

35803.q: What does freedom of assembly allow?
35803.e: People may meet peacefully, for example for a demonstration. This is a fundamental right in the Federal Constitution.

35804.q: What does the right to privacy protect?
35804.e: Privacy protects, for example, your home, letters and personal data. Strangers may not simply snoop around in them.
35804.m: My personal life is protected by the right to privacy.

35805.q: What do you get through the right to help in situations of need?
35805.e: Anyone in need who cannot help themselves gets help. This includes food, shelter and medical care.
35805.m: Anyone in need has a right to help to survive.

35806.q: What does freedom of residence allow Swiss citizens to do?
35806.e: Swiss citizens may settle anywhere in the country. So you may choose freely which municipality you live in.
35806.m: Swiss citizens may live in any municipality in the country.

35807.q: Why can the Federal Constitution be compared with the house rules of a block of flats?
a: It contains the most important rules
It regulates the rubbish in the building
35807.e: House rules govern living together in a building. The Federal Constitution governs living together in the whole country.
35807.m: The Federal Constitution is like Switzerland's house rules.

35808.q: Who must keep to the Federal Constitution?
35808.e: The Federal Constitution applies to all people and also to the authorities. No law may go against it.
35808.m: Everyone must keep to the Federal Constitution, including the authorities.

35809.q: Who must agree when the Federal Constitution is changed?
35809.e: Changing the Federal Constitution requires a vote. The majority of the people and of the cantons must say Yes.
35809.m: The constitution is only changed if the people and the cantons agree.

35810.q: With which words does the Federal Constitution begin?
a: In the name of Almighty God!
35810.e: The Federal Constitution begins with a solemn introduction. Its first words are “In the name of Almighty God!”.
35810.m: The Federal Constitution begins with a solemn introduction.

35811.q: What is the introduction to the Federal Constitution called?
35811.e: The preamble comes right at the start of the Federal Constitution. It explains what the state wants to achieve.
35811.m: The introduction to the Federal Constitution is called the preamble.

35812.q: According to the preamble, by what is the strength of a people measured?
a: The wellbeing of its weakest members
35812.e: The introduction to the Federal Constitution says that the strength of a people is measured by the wellbeing of its weakest members. A society is strong when it looks after the weak.
35812.m: A people is strong when the weak are doing well.

35813.q: Into which sections is the Federal Constitution divided?
35813.e: The Federal Constitution consists of many numbered articles. Each article deals with a particular topic.
35813.m: The Federal Constitution is divided into numbered articles.

35814.q: Where can anyone read the Federal Constitution for free?
35814.e: The Federal Constitution is public. You can read it free of charge on the Confederation's website, for example.
35814.m: The Federal Constitution is freely available to everyone.

35815.q: What do you normally get for voluntary work?
35815.e: Voluntary work is done without pay. You help because you want to do something good for the community.
35815.m: Voluntary work is done without pay.

35816.q: Which is an example of voluntary work?
35816.e: Many coaches in clubs work without pay. Without them, many clubs would not exist.

35817.q: Where do young people voluntarily lead groups of children?
35817.e: In the Scouts and in youth organisations, young people lead the groups. They do this voluntarily in their free time.
35817.m: In the Scouts, young people voluntarily lead groups of children.

35818.q: What is the document called in which you can have voluntary work recorded?
35818.e: The volunteer certificate records where you have helped voluntarily. This can be useful when applying for a job.
35818.m: In a volunteer certificate you can record your voluntary work.

35819.q: On which day is International Volunteer Day?
35819.e: The UN declared 5 December Volunteer Day. On this day volunteers are thanked.

35820.q: How can a child help voluntarily in the neighbourhood?
35820.e: Small acts of help in the neighbourhood are voluntary work too. For example, you can go shopping for an elderly person.
35820.m: Even small acts of help in the neighbourhood are valuable.

35821.q: What is a voluntary position called, for example on the committee of a club?
35821.e: An honorary post is a task you take on voluntarily and usually without pay. Many club committees work on an honorary basis.
35821.m: You take on an honorary post voluntarily.

35822.q: How many days of unpaid leave a year may young employees up to 30 take for youth work?
35822.e: The law allows young employees up to the age of 30 youth leave of up to one working week a year. That way they can lead a camp, for example.
35822.m: Young employees may take leave for voluntary youth work.

a: Looking after something and standing by it
35823.e: Anyone who takes responsibility looks after a task. They also stand by it if something goes wrong.
35823.m: Responsibility means looking after something and standing by it.

35824.q: What do you do if you have accidentally broken something?
35824.e: Everyone makes mistakes. Anyone who takes responsibility admits the mistake and helps to put it right.
35824.m: If you make a mistake, admit it and apologise.

35825.q: Who is responsible for a pet?
35825.e: A pet needs food, water and care every day. Its owners are responsible for this.
35825.m: Anyone who has a pet looks after it well every day.

35826.q: How do you take responsibility for the environment at a picnic?
a: Throw your rubbish in the water
35826.e: Rubbish belongs in the bin or back home with you. That way meadows and forests stay clean.
35826.m: I always take my rubbish with me or put it in the bin.

35827.q: What does the Federal Constitution require of every person?
a: Responsibility for themselves and the community
Living in the same canton all their life
Being a member of a party
35827.e: The Federal Constitution says that every person takes responsibility for themselves and contributes as far as they can to the wellbeing of the community.
35827.m: Every person is responsible for themselves and for the community.

35828.q: What shows that a child is taking responsibility in the class?
a: They do their class job reliably
35828.e: Anyone who does their tasks reliably shows responsibility. The others can then rely on them.
35828.m: You can rely on people who take responsibility.

35829.q: What do you do if a younger child falls over in the playground and cries?
a: Pretend I have not seen anything
35829.e: Anyone who notices and helps takes responsibility for others. An adult can then help further.
35829.m: If someone needs help, I do not look away.

35830.q: What is a child partly responsible for when cycling on the road?
a: Their own safety and that of others
35830.e: Anyone who rides a bike follows the rules of the road. That way you protect yourself and others on the road.
35830.m: In traffic I am responsible for myself and for others.

35831.q: What do you say when someone gives you something?
35831.e: By saying “Thank you” you show that you are pleased with the present. That is a sign of respect.

35832.q: What do you do before going into someone else's room?
35832.e: If you knock, the person in the room can say yes or no first. That way you respect their privacy.
35832.m: At a closed door you knock first.

35833.q: How do you show respect when someone is talking to you?
35833.e: Listening shows the other person that their words matter. Listening is a simple form of respect.
35833.m: Listening well is a sign of respect.

35835.q: What does it mean when you say “please”?
35835.e: The word “please” makes a question or a wish friendly. That way you treat others with respect.
35835.m: With the word please, you ask politely.

35836.q: How do you treat other children's things?
35836.e: Other people's things belong to someone else. If you treat them carefully and give them back, you show respect.
35836.m: You treat other people's things carefully.

35837.q: What do you do if an older person has no seat on a full bus?
a: Put your bag on the seat
35837.e: Older people often find standing harder. If you offer your seat, you are being considerate and showing respect.
35837.m: On the bus you offer older people a seat.

35838.q: What is respectful when another child cannot do something?
35838.e: Every child learns at their own pace. Helping instead of laughing treats the other child with respect.
35838.m: Helping instead of laughing shows respect.

a: Letting others be as they are
35839.e: Tolerance means accepting other opinions, habits or ways of life. You do not have to like everything, but you allow it.
35839.m: Tolerant people let others be as they are.

35840.q: A child does not eat pork. What is tolerant?
35840.e: People do not eat certain things for different reasons, for example because of their religion. Being tolerant means simply accepting this.
35840.m: You accept what others do not want to eat.

35841.q: A child in your class prefers skipping to football at break time. What is tolerant?
a: Not talking to them any more
35841.e: Every child has their own favourite games. Being tolerant means simply accepting that.
35841.m: Others may have different favourite games.

35842.q: Your friend has a different favourite colour from you. What is right?
35842.e: People have different preferences. Tolerance means taking that calmly.

35843.q: What is the opposite of tolerance?
35843.e: The prefix “in-” means “not” here. Intolerance means not accepting others.
35843.m: The opposite of tolerance is intolerance.

35844.q: What may every person in Switzerland choose freely?
35844.e: Freedom of religion is in the Federal Constitution. Everyone may believe what they want, or belong to no religion at all.
35844.m: In Switzerland everyone may choose their religion freely.

35845.q: What is tolerant when a child speaks differently from you because they have a different mother tongue?
35845.e: Anyone learning a new language still makes mistakes. Listening patiently helps them and is tolerant.
35845.m: Anyone learning a language deserves patience.

35846.q: Do you have to agree with everyone?
a: No, and you may insult people
35846.e: Different opinions are normal. What matters is that you still treat each other kindly and without insults.
35846.m: You may disagree and still stay friendly.

35847.q: What do you call a child who helps other children find a solution when they quarrel?
35847.e: Peer mediators are trained at many schools. They help those who are quarrelling to find a solution themselves.
35847.m: Peer mediators help others to settle a quarrel.

35848.q: Whose side does a good peer mediator take?
35848.e: A peer mediator is neutral. She does not take either side, so that both can trust her.
35848.m: A peer mediator does not take sides.

35849.e: In an I-message you say, for example, “I am sad because ...”. That way you do not attack the other person.
35849.m: In an I-message you say how you yourself feel.

35850.q: What can help if you are very angry during a quarrel?
35850.e: Breathing deeply calms the body. Afterwards you can talk better and find a solution.
35850.m: Taking deep breaths helps with strong anger.

35851.q: Which rule applies in a mediation talk?
35851.e: Each side may tell their story without being interrupted. That way both feel taken seriously.
35851.m: In mediation you let each other finish.

35852.q: What is never allowed in a quarrel?
35852.e: Violence does not solve a quarrel; it makes it worse and hurts. You may argue, but only with words.
35852.m: In a quarrel you never hit.

35853.q: What do you call a solution that both sides are happy with?
35853.e: In an agreement both sides gain something. That is why such a solution usually lasts a long time.
35853.m: A good agreement makes both sides happy.

35854.q: What do people often do at the end of a mediation once they have agreed?
35854.e: A handshake shows that the quarrel is over and both want to keep to the agreement.

35855.q: Who can you ask for help if you cannot settle a quarrel yourselves?
35855.e: Teachers know the children and can help settle quarrels. It is right to get help.
35855.m: In a difficult quarrel you may ask a teacher for help.

35856.q: What is the peace bridge at school for?
35856.e: The peace bridge is a model that children use to settle a quarrel step by step. The bridge is a picture of finding your way back to each other.
35856.m: On the peace bridge, children settle a quarrel.

35857.q: Where do the two quarrelling children stand at the start of the peace bridge?
35857.e: At the start the two stand far apart, just like their opinions. With every step they come closer.
35857.m: At the start, the two sides stand at the two ends of the bridge.

35858.q: When may a child take a step forward on the peace bridge?
a: When a step of the conversation is done
35858.e: On the peace bridge you only move on once you have, for example, listened or said how you feel. That way every step is earned.
35858.m: On the peace bridge you move forward step by step by talking.

35859.q: What does a child on the peace bridge do after the other child has told their side?
35859.e: Repeating what the other person said shows that you listened well. That way you also understand the other side.
35859.m: On the peace bridge you repeat what the other person said.

35860.q: What does the picture of the bridge show in the peace bridge?
a: You build a path to each other
35860.e: A quarrel separates people like a ditch. The bridge connects the two sides again.
35860.m: The peace bridge connects two children after a quarrel.

35861.q: Where do the two children meet at the end of the peace bridge?
35861.e: After all the steps, the two meet in the middle of the bridge. There they make peace.
35861.m: In the middle of the peace bridge, the children make peace.

35862.q: Which question do you ask yourself on the peace bridge when looking for a solution?
35862.e: When looking for a solution you look forward. Each child thinks about what they can contribute and what they would like from the other.
35862.m: On the peace bridge you ask what you can contribute to the solution.

35863.q: Who often accompanies the children on the peace bridge?
a: A peer mediator or a teacher
35863.e: A neutral person leads the conversation and makes sure the rules are kept. This can be trained children or teachers.
35863.m: A neutral person accompanies the children on the peace bridge.

a: A smaller group in a country
35864.e: A minority is a group that has fewer members than others, for example because of its language. Its rights must be specially protected.
35864.m: A minority is a smaller group in a country.

35865.q: In the class almost everyone wants to play football, but three children prefer dodgeball. What is considerate?
35865.e: Even when the majority decides, the wishes of the few should not always be forgotten. Taking turns is considerate towards the minority.
35865.m: The wishes of a minority deserve attention too.

35866.q: In which canton is Romansh mainly spoken?
35866.e: Romansh is one of the three official languages of the canton of Grisons, along with German and Italian.
35866.m: Romansh is mainly spoken in the Grisons.

a: So that they have equal rights
35867.e: Otherwise the majority could simply decide for the minority. Protection makes sure small groups keep their rights too.
35867.m: Protecting minorities secures equal rights for them.

35868.q: Which people in Switzerland are recognised as a national minority and partly live a travelling life?
35868.e: Switzerland recognises the Yenish and Sinti as a national minority. Some of them travel in summer and move around in caravans.
35868.m: The Yenish and Sinti are a recognised minority in Switzerland.

35869.q: What protects minorities in Switzerland from the majority simply deciding for them?
35869.e: The fundamental rights in the Federal Constitution apply to all people. They also protect small groups from the majority.
35869.m: Fundamental rights apply to minorities too.

35870.q: Only one child in the class speaks Italian. What is right?
35870.e: Every language is valuable. The child may keep their language and learn German at the same time.
35870.m: Every child may keep their mother tongue.

35871.q: One child is the only left-hander in the class. What is considerate?
35871.e: Most things are made for right-handers. With suitable tools, a left-handed child can join in well too.
35871.m: Even a few children with special needs deserve consideration.

35872.e: Diversity means that people are different, for example in appearance, language or faith. That makes life colourful.
35872.m: Diversity means there are many different kinds.

35873.q: Which festival do many Muslims celebrate at the end of the fasting month of Ramadan?
35873.e: After the fasting month of Ramadan, Muslims celebrate the festival of breaking the fast. In German-speaking countries it is also called the Sugar Festival.
35873.m: After Ramadan, Muslims celebrate Eid al-Fitr.

35874.q: Which Jewish festival is celebrated for eight days with candles on a candlestick?
35874.e: At Hanukkah one more candle is lit each evening. At the end, eight candles are burning.
35874.m: Hanukkah is the Jewish festival of lights.

35875.q: Which festival of lights do many Hindus celebrate?
35875.e: Diwali is the great festival of lights in Hinduism. People light lots of small lamps.
35875.m: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights.

35876.q: Roughly how many people in Switzerland do not have a Swiss passport (as of 2025)?
35876.e: According to the Federal Statistical Office, around 28 per cent of the population had no Swiss passport at the end of 2025, about one person in four. Many of them have lived here for a long time.
35876.m: In Switzerland, about one person in four has no Swiss passport.

35877.q: Why is diversity in a class good?
a: You can learn from each other
35877.e: Children with different experiences bring different ideas. That way everyone learns something new.
35877.m: In a diverse class, you learn from each other.

35878.q: Whose birth do Christians celebrate at Christmas?
35878.e: At Christmas, Christians celebrate the birth of Jesus. In Switzerland, 25 December is a public holiday.
35878.m: At Christmas people celebrate the birth of Jesus.

35879.q: What do all people have in common despite their differences?
35879.e: People look different and speak different languages. Even so, every person is of equal worth.
35879.m: Every person has the same dignity.

35880.e: Inclusion means that everyone can take part, including people with a disability. Nobody is left out.

35881.q: What do blind people often use to read texts?
35881.e: The writing system for blind people is called Braille. You feel small dots with your fingers.
35881.m: Blind people read Braille with their fingers.

35882.q: What is the maximum number of dots in a Braille character?
35882.e: Each Braille character has room for six dots in two columns. Different dots are raised depending on the letter.
35882.m: A Braille character has six dots.

35883.q: How do many deaf people communicate?
35883.e: In sign language you speak with your hands, face and body. In German-speaking Switzerland there is Swiss German Sign Language for this.
35883.m: Deaf people often communicate in sign language.

35884.q: What helps people in wheelchairs to get into a building?
35884.e: Stairs are an obstacle for wheelchairs. Ramps and lifts make buildings accessible to everyone.
35884.m: A ramp makes a building accessible for wheelchairs.

35885.q: Which animal helps blind people to find their way safely?
35885.e: Guide dogs are specially trained. They lead their owners around obstacles.
35885.m: A guide dog leads blind people safely.

35886.q: What are the Olympic Games for athletes with a physical disability called?
35886.e: The Paralympic Games take place shortly after the Olympic Games. Athletes with disabilities compete against each other there.
35886.m: Athletes with disabilities compete at the Paralympics.

35887.q: What helps a child in a wheelchair to reach every floor of the school?
35887.e: You cannot go up stairs in a wheelchair. With a lift, the child can reach every floor and join in everywhere.
35887.m: A lift helps children in wheelchairs reach the upper floor.

35888.q: A child in a wheelchair wants to join in a game. What is inclusive?
a: Changing the game so they can join in
35888.e: Inclusion means adapting the rules so that everyone can take part. That way every child enjoys the game.
35888.m: You can adapt a game so that everyone can join in.

35889.q: What should you do if you see a child being bullied?
35889.e: If you see bullying, you can help by telling adults. That is not telling tales, it is helping.
35889.m: If you see bullying, get help from adults.

35890.q: Is it telling tales if you tell a teacher about bullying?
a: Yes, if the child does not want it
No, but you may only tell your parents
35890.e: Telling tales means wanting to harm someone. Reporting bullying means wanting to protect someone, and that is right.
35890.m: Reporting bullying is helping, not telling tales.

35891.q: How can children help who see another child being bullied?
a: Not laughing along and getting help
35891.e: Onlookers can change a lot. If they stop laughing along and get help, bullying often stops.

35892.q: What can you show a child who is being bullied?
a: That it is their own fault
35892.e: Children who are bullied often feel lonely. Standing by them gives them courage.
35892.m: Show a bullied child that they are not alone.

35893.q: Who is to blame when a child is bullied?
35893.e: A child is never to blame for being bullied. The responsibility lies with those who torment them.
35893.m: A bullied child is never to blame.

35894.q: What can you do if you get nasty messages in a chat?
a: Take a screenshot and show an adult
35894.e: A screenshot gives you proof. Adults can then help stop the cyberbullying.
35894.m: Save nasty messages and show them to adults.

a: Leaving someone out again and again
35895.e: Anyone who deliberately and repeatedly does not let a child join in is bullying them. Bullying can happen without hitting too.
35895.m: Deliberately leaving someone out can be bullying too.

35896.q: How do bullied children often feel?
35896.e: Anyone who is tormented again and again often feels sad and is afraid to go to school. That is why it is important to stop bullying.
35896.m: Bullying frightens children and must be stopped.

35897.e: In neighbourly help, people who live close to each other support one another. For example, they do shopping for each other.
35897.m: In neighbourly help, neighbours help each other.

35898.q: Your neighbour is on holiday. How can you help?
35898.e: When neighbours go away, you can water their plants or empty the letterbox. Of course, only if they have asked you to.
35898.m: During the holidays you can water the plants for your neighbours.

35899.q: How can you help a sick elderly neighbour?
a: Ring his doorbell and run away
35899.e: People who are ill often cannot do their own shopping. Doing it for them helps a lot.
35899.m: You can do the shopping for sick neighbours.

35900.q: In which month do many places celebrate Neighbours' Day?
35900.e: Neighbours' Day takes place in spring in many countries, including Switzerland, usually at the end of May. Neighbours then meet to eat and chat.
35900.m: Neighbours' Day is usually in May.

35901.q: What friendly thing can you say to a new family in the building?
35901.e: New neighbours do not know anyone yet. A friendly welcome helps them feel at home.
35901.m: You give new neighbours a warm welcome.

35902.q: The neighbours' cat needs looking after for a week. What is neighbourly help?
35902.e: When neighbours are away, their pet still needs food. Feeding it helps the neighbours.
35902.m: You can feed the neighbours' pet.

35903.q: What can you do for elderly neighbours in winter?
a: Shovel the snow in front of the house
35903.e: Older people slip more easily on snow and ice. Shovelling snow makes the path safer.
35903.m: In winter you can shovel snow for your neighbours.

35904.q: What do you do with a parcel that was left with you for the neighbours?
35904.e: The parcel belongs to the neighbours. Passing it on helps them and is honest.
35904.m: You take a parcel for the neighbours round to them.

35905.q: Which figure is a well-known symbol of justice?
35905.e: Justitia is a woman with scales and a sword. She often stands outside courts or on fountains, for example in Bern.
35905.m: Justitia is the symbol of justice.

35906.q: What does Justitia hold in her hand to show that both sides are weighed equally?
35906.e: The scales show that both sides are examined carefully. Only then is a decision made.
35906.m: Justitia's scales stand for weighing things up fairly.

35907.q: Why does Justitia often wear a blindfold?
a: The same rules apply to everyone
35907.e: The blindfold shows that Justitia does not look at who is standing in front of her. It does not matter whether someone is rich or poor: the same rules apply to everyone.
35907.m: The blindfold shows that the same rules apply to everyone.

35908.q: Three children share 12 cherries fairly. How many does each child get?
35908.e: 12 cherries divided by 3 children is 4 cherries each. That way everyone gets the same amount.
35908.m: Sharing fairly gives everyone the same amount.

35909.q: A child has forgotten their morning snack. What is fair and kind?
35909.e: Sharing makes sure nobody stays hungry. Sharing is a sign of fairness and friendship.
35909.m: Sharing your snack is fair and kind.

35910.q: In a race, a much younger child may start a bit further ahead. Why is that fair?
a: Otherwise they would not have an equal chance
35910.e: Fair does not always mean treating everyone exactly the same. Sometimes someone needs help to have the same chance.
35910.m: It is fair when everyone gets an equal chance.

35911.q: Who makes sure in Switzerland that a dispute in court is decided fairly?
35911.e: Courts examine what happened and decide according to the law. That way justice should apply to everyone.
35911.m: Courts decide according to the law.

35912.q: Two children are arguing over the last piece of cake. What is a fair solution?
a: One child cuts, the other chooses
35912.e: Whoever cuts tries hard to make pieces the same size, because the other child chooses first. That way it is fair for both.
35912.m: One cuts and the other chooses: that is how you share fairly.

35913.e: Honest people tell the truth, even when it is hard. That is why you can trust them.

35914.q: Which storybook character's nose grows when he lies?
35914.e: Pinocchio is a wooden puppet from an Italian book. Every time he lies, his nose gets longer.
35914.m: Pinocchio's nose grows with every lie.

35915.q: How does the German saying “Lies have ...” continue?
35915.e: The German saying “Lies have short legs” means that lies usually come out quickly. With short legs you do not get far.
35915.m: In German they say lies have short legs.

35916.q: You have accidentally broken a vase. What is honest?
35916.e: Admitting a mistake is honest. It is usually less bad than a lie that comes out later.

35917.q: You find a purse in the street. What is honest?
35917.e: The purse belongs to someone else. At the police station or the lost property office the person can collect it again.
35917.m: You hand in things you find.

35918.q: What is dishonest in a test?
35918.e: Copying means passing off someone else's work as your own. That is not honest.
35918.m: Copying in a test is dishonest.

35919.q: Why is honesty important in a friendship?
a: So that you can trust each other
35919.e: Friends must be able to rely on each other. Without honesty, trust is lost.

35920.q: The shop assistant gives you too much change. What is honest?
35920.e: The extra money belongs to the shop. Giving it back is honest.
35920.m: You give back too much change.

35921.q: May girls and boys in Switzerland train for the same jobs?
35921.e: Girls and boys have the same rights. Every job is open to everyone, for example carpenter or nurse.
35921.m: Girls and boys may train for any job.

35922.q: Which sentence has been in the Swiss Federal Constitution since 1981?
a: Men and women have equal rights
Only men may become Federal Councillors
Women need their husband's permission to take a job
35922.e: Since 1981 the Federal Constitution has stated that men and women have equal rights. This applies in the family, in education and at work.
35922.m: The Federal Constitution states that men and women have equal rights.

35923.q: Who should help with the housework, girls or boys?
35923.e: Housework is not just a job for girls or women. In a fair family, everyone helps.
35923.m: Girls and boys both help with the housework.

35924.q: What does the UN International Day of the Girl campaign for?
35924.e: The UN introduced an International Day of the Girl. It draws attention to the fact that girls everywhere should have the same chances as boys, for example in education.
35924.m: The International Day of the Girl campaigns for girls' rights.

35925.q: What is the name of the first woman elected to the Swiss Federal Council?
35925.e: Elisabeth Kopp was elected to the Federal Council in 1984 as the first woman. Today women and men work together in the government.
35925.m: Elisabeth Kopp was Switzerland's first woman Federal Councillor.

35926.q: Which big women's football tournament took place in Switzerland in summer 2025?
35926.e: In July 2025 the Women's European Football Championship took place in Switzerland. Many girls and women love playing football.
35926.m: The Women's Euro 2025 took place in Switzerland.

35928.q: A boy wants to learn to dance, a girl wants to play ice hockey. What is right?
35928.e: Hobbies are not just for girls or just for boys. Every child may do what they enjoy.
35928.m: Every child may choose their hobby freely.

a: A territory, a people and a government
A high mountain and a big lake
A port and lots of ships
35929.e: A state has a territory with borders, people who live there and a government that makes decisions. It does not need mountains, lakes or kings.
35929.m: A state consists of territory, people and government.

35930.q: What are people called who belong to a country and have its passport?
35930.e: Anyone who belongs to a country is one of its citizens. Only they get that country’s passport.

35931.q: What is a country without a sea coast, like Switzerland, called?
35931.e: Switzerland does not border any sea; it lies in the middle of the continent. Such countries are called landlocked countries.
35931.m: Switzerland is a landlocked country with no sea.

35932.q: What is a country completely surrounded by sea, like Iceland, called?
35932.e: Iceland lies on an island in the Atlantic. A country on one or more islands is called an island state.
35932.m: An island state is completely surrounded by sea.

35933.q: What is a country that consists almost entirely of a single city, like Singapore, called?
35933.e: Singapore is both a city and a state of its own. That is why it is called a city state.
35933.m: A city state is a city that is its own country.

35934.q: Which country code is shown on the back of Swiss cars when they drive abroad?
35934.e: The code CH shows that a car comes from Switzerland. It is also used in internet addresses such as “.ch”.
35934.m: Swiss cars carry the code CH.

35935.q: What does the code “CH” for Switzerland stand for?
35935.e: CH is the abbreviation of the Latin name Confoederatio Helvetica. Latin was chosen because Switzerland has four national languages.
35935.m: CH stands for Confoederatio Helvetica in Latin.

35936.e: The official name is written in the Federal Constitution: Swiss Confederation. Switzerland is not a kingdom.
35936.m: Switzerland’s official name is the Swiss Confederation.

a: The line where a country ends
35937.e: A national border separates two countries from each other. On one side the laws of one country apply, on the other side those of the other.
35937.m: At the national border one country ends and the next begins.

35938.q: Roughly how long is the border around Switzerland?
35938.e: Switzerland’s national border is about 1,935 kilometres long. It runs through mountains, forests, lakes and rivers.
35938.m: The Swiss border is almost 2,000 kilometres long.

35939.q: How is a national border often marked in forests or on meadows?
35939.e: Boundary stones show exactly where the border runs. Often letters or coats of arms of the countries are carved on both sides.
35939.m: Boundary stones show where the border runs.

35940.q: Who checks at the Swiss border what is brought into the country?
35940.e: Customs officers work at the border. They check the people and goods coming into Switzerland.
35940.m: Customs carry out checks at the border.

a: A place where you travel into another country
A car park by the lake
35941.e: At a border crossing a road or path leads from one country into another. There it is possible to check who and what is crossing the border.
35941.m: At a border crossing you travel from one country into another.

35942.q: Who checks at the Swiss border which goods come into the country?
35942.e: In Switzerland the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security is responsible for this. It checks goods and people too.
35942.m: Customs check goods at the border.

35943.q: What should you always have with you when you travel across a border?
35943.e: With your passport or identity card you can show who you are. This can be asked for at any border.
35943.m: Always travel across a border with an identity document.

35944.q: What is the building at a border crossing where customs officers work called?
35944.e: At the customs office goods are declared and duties are paid. In the past there was such a building at almost every border crossing.
35944.m: Customs officers work in the customs office.

35945.q: What is the barrier that used to block the road at many border crossings called?
35945.e: The boom barrier is a pole across the road. It was only raised once the check was over.
35945.m: In the past a boom barrier blocked the road at the border.

35946.q: Which animals help customs find banned things in luggage?
35946.e: Dogs have a very sensitive nose. Specially trained sniffer dogs can smell drugs or money in luggage, for example.
35946.m: Sniffer dogs help customs with their sensitive noses.

35947.q: What do you have to do at customs if you have bought more than you may bring in duty-free?
35947.e: Anyone who buys too much has to declare the goods at customs and pay duty. Anyone who does not can get a fine.
35947.m: If you have bought too much, declare it at customs.

35948.q: Which word is written at border crossings into Italy for “customs”?
35948.e: In Italian, customs is called “dogana”. In French it is “douane”.

35949.q: How long is a Swiss passport valid for adults?
35949.e: From the age of 18 a Swiss passport is valid for 10 years. After that you have to apply for a new one.
35949.m: For adults a Swiss passport is valid for 10 years.

35950.q: How long is a Swiss passport valid for children?
35950.e: For children and young people under 18 the passport is valid for 5 years. Children’s appearance changes faster than adults’.
35950.m: Children’s passports are valid for 5 years.

35951.q: Does a child need their own identity document for a trip abroad?
35951.e: Every child needs their own passport or identity card. Children can no longer be entered in their parents’ passport.
35951.m: Even babies need their own identity document.

35952.q: What is stored in the chip of a Swiss passport, among other things?
35952.e: The chip contains the data from the passport and the photo, and for people aged 12 and over also the fingerprints. This makes the passport hard to forge.
35952.m: The chip in the passport stores the person’s photo.

35953.q: Where do you apply for a new passport in Switzerland?
35953.e: You make an appointment at the passport office or ID centre of your canton. A photo and fingerprints are taken there.
35953.m: You apply for a passport at the cantonal passport office.

35954.e: Some countries require a visa before you are allowed in. It is often stuck into the passport or issued electronically.
35954.m: A visa allows you to enter a country.

35955.q: For which destination do Swiss people need a passport instead of an identity card?
35955.e: For many countries in Europe an identity card is enough. But for the USA you need a passport.
