35955.m: You need a passport for the USA.

35956.q: What can be seen on the cover of a Swiss passport?
35956.e: The Swiss cross is shown on the red cover of the Swiss passport. It is the symbol of Switzerland.
35956.m: The Swiss cross is shown on the Swiss passport.

35957.q: What is the identity card in Switzerland often called for short?
35957.e: The identity card is usually just called the ID. It is an official identity document.
35957.m: The identity card is called ID for short.

35958.q: Roughly how big is the Swiss identity card?
a: As big as a bank card
As big as an exercise book
35958.e: The ID is the size of a bank card. That is why it fits nicely into a purse or wallet.
35958.m: The ID fits into a wallet like a bank card.

35959.q: Where can you travel with a Swiss identity card?
a: To every country in the world
35959.e: With the ID you can travel to all EU countries and other European countries. For many other countries you need a passport.
35959.m: With the ID you can travel through a large part of Europe.

35960.q: What is written on the Swiss identity card?
a: Name, date of birth and photo
35960.e: The ID shows your name, date of birth, height and place of origin, as well as a photo. In this way you can show who you are.
35960.m: The ID shows name, date of birth and photo.

35961.q: What do you need an identity card for?
35961.e: Identity means who someone is. With the ID you can prove this officially, for example at the border.
35961.m: With the ID you prove who you are.

35962.q: What should you do if you have lost your identity card?
a: Report the loss to the police
35962.e: A lost identity document must be reported to the police. That way nobody else can misuse it, and you can order a new ID.
35962.m: Report a lost identity document to the police.

35963.q: From what age can a child in Switzerland get their own identity card?
35963.e: Even babies can get their own ID. The parents apply for it for their child.
35963.m: Even babies can have their own ID.

35964.q: What is one difference between a passport and an identity card?
a: The passport is a booklet, the ID is a card
The ID is red, the passport white
Only the passport has a photo
The ID is only valid in Switzerland
35964.e: The passport is a small booklet with pages for stamps and visas. The ID is a solid card without pages.
35964.m: The passport is a booklet, the ID is a card.

a: The city where the government is based
The oldest city in a country
The city by the highest mountain
35965.e: The government and parliament of a country usually work in the capital. It is not always the biggest city.
35965.m: The country’s government is based in the capital.

35966.q: What is Bern officially called in Switzerland?
35966.e: The Federal Constitution does not name a capital. Bern is officially called the federal city, because the Federal Council and Parliament are based there.

35967.q: Which city is the biggest in Switzerland but not the federal city?
35967.e: Zurich has the most inhabitants. But the government and parliament are based in Bern.
35967.m: Zurich is the biggest city, Bern the federal city.

35968.q: What is the capital of China?
35968.e: Beijing, once also known in English as Peking, is the capital of China. The famous Forbidden City stands there.
35968.m: Beijing is the capital of China.

35969.q: In Switzerland, what is the town where a cantonal government is based called?
35969.e: Every canton has a cantonal capital, for example Chur in the Grisons or Sion in Valais. The cantonal government works there.
35969.m: The cantonal government is based in the cantonal capital.

a: The flag that stands for a country
The flag of a sports club
35970.e: Every country has its own national flag with particular colours and symbols. It is a symbol of the whole country.
35970.m: The national flag is the symbol of a country.

35971.q: On which day are there especially many Swiss flags hanging in Switzerland?
35971.e: 1 August is Swiss National Day. Many houses are then decorated with Swiss flags.
35971.m: On 1 August many Swiss flags decorate the country.

35972.q: What does it mean when a flag is only raised halfway?
35972.e: A flag flown halfway up is at half-mast. This shows mourning, for example when an important person has died.
35972.m: A flag at half-mast shows mourning.

35973.q: What is the tall pole on which a flag is raised called?
35973.e: The flag is pulled up the flagpole with a rope. Many municipal buildings and schools have one.
35973.m: The flag hangs on the flagpole.

35974.q: Which flag is raised at the Olympic Games when an athlete wins gold?
35974.e: At the medal ceremony the flags of the medal winners’ countries are raised. For gold, the national anthem is played as well.
35974.m: When someone wins Olympic gold, their country’s flag flies.

35975.q: What are the four arms of the cross on the Swiss flag like?
a: Longer at the top than at the bottom
35975.e: The Swiss cross has four arms of equal length. Each arm is a little longer than it is wide.
35975.m: The Swiss cross has four arms of equal length.

35976.q: What does the flag flying at the back of a big ship show?
a: Which country the ship comes from
How many passengers are on board
35976.e: Every sea-going ship sails under the flag of a country. Switzerland also has sea-going ships with the Swiss flag.
35976.m: The flag on a ship shows its home country.

35977.q: How many cantons, each with its own cantonal flag, does Switzerland have?
35977.e: Switzerland is made up of 26 cantons. Each canton has its own coat of arms and its own flag.
35977.m: Switzerland has 26 cantons with their own flags.

a: A solemn song for a country
35978.e: Every country has its own anthem. It is played and sung at celebrations and important occasions.
35978.m: The national anthem is a country’s solemn song.

35980.q: When do you often hear national anthems on television?
35980.e: Before an international match the anthems of both teams are played. The players stand in a line.
35980.m: Before international matches the anthems of both countries are played.

35981.q: What do people usually do when the national anthem is played?
35981.e: Out of respect people stand up and listen quietly or sing along. In this way they show respect for the country.
35981.m: During the anthem you stand up and keep quiet.

35982.q: In how many national languages is there a text of the Swiss Psalm?
35982.e: The Swiss Psalm exists in German, French, Italian and Romansh. These are the four national languages.
35982.m: The Swiss Psalm is sung in four national languages.

35983.q: What is a head of state?
a: The person who represents a country
The best teacher in the country
The boss of the biggest company
The oldest person in the country
35983.e: The head of state represents a country towards other countries. For example, they receive guests from abroad.
35983.m: The head of state represents their country.

35984.q: What is the title of the person who chairs the Swiss Federal Council each year?
35984.e: One member of the Federal Council becomes President of the Confederation for one year. This person chairs the meetings and represents Switzerland.
35984.m: The President of the Confederation chairs the Federal Council.

35985.q: Who in Switzerland actually forms the head of state together?
35985.e: The seven members of the Federal Council together form the government and the head of state. The President of the Confederation is only the first among equals.
35985.m: In Switzerland the whole Federal Council forms the head of state.

35986.q: Who is the head of state in a kingdom?
35986.e: In a monarchy the queen or king is the head of state. The role is usually passed down within the family.
35986.m: In a kingdom the monarch is head of state.

35987.q: Roughly how many countries are there in the world?
35987.e: Usually around 195 states are counted. These include the 193 UN members, Vatican City and Palestine.
35987.m: There are around 195 countries in the world.

35988.q: On which continent are there the most countries?
35988.e: There are 54 states in Africa, more than on any other continent. Asia is bigger but has fewer countries.
35988.m: Africa is the continent with the most countries.

35989.q: On which continent are there no countries?
35989.e: Antarctica at the South Pole is covered in ice. There are no states there, only research stations, and a treaty makes sure it is used peacefully for research.
35989.m: There are no countries in Antarctica.

35990.q: Which country has the most inhabitants (as of 2025)?
35990.e: In 2023 India overtook China. Both countries have more than 1.4 billion inhabitants.
35990.m: India is the country with the most people.

35991.q: Which is the largest country by area in the Americas?
35991.e: Canada lies in the north of the Americas and covers a huge area. It is even slightly bigger than the USA.
35991.m: Canada is the largest country in the Americas.

35992.q: Which country is the youngest state in the world, independent since 2011?
35992.e: South Sudan separated from Sudan in 2011. Since then it has been a state of its own and a member of the UN.
35992.m: South Sudan has been the youngest state since 2011.

35993.q: Why can’t the number of countries be given exactly?
a: Not all countries are recognised everywhere
The number changes a lot every year
35993.e: Some territories, such as Kosovo or Taiwan, are recognised as countries by only some states. That is why people usually say “about 195”.
35993.m: Not every country is recognised by all the others.

35994.q: Which is the largest country in the world?
35994.e: With about 17 million square kilometres, Russia is the largest country on Earth by area. It is almost as big as the whole of South America.
35994.m: Russia is the largest country in the world.

35995.q: What is the capital of Russia?
35995.e: Moscow is the capital and largest city of Russia. St Petersburg used to be the capital.
35995.m: Moscow is the capital of Russia.

35996.q: On which two continents does Russia lie?
35996.e: About a quarter of its area lies in Europe, the largest part in Asia. That is why Russia belongs to two continents.
35996.m: Russia lies in Europe and Asia.

35997.q: How many time zones does Russia have?
35997.e: Russia is so wide from west to east that it has 11 time zones. When it is evening in Moscow, it is already the next morning in the east.

35998.q: What colours is the flag of Russia?
35998.e: The Russian flag has three horizontal stripes. White is at the top, blue in the middle and red at the bottom.
35998.m: The flag of Russia is white, blue and red.

35999.q: What is the famous long railway line across Russia called?
35999.e: The Trans-Siberian Railway runs from Moscow to Vladivostok on the Pacific. The line is over 9,000 kilometres long.
35999.m: The Trans-Siberian Railway crosses the whole of Russia.

36000.q: Roughly how many times would Switzerland fit into Russia?
36000.e: Russia has about 17 million square kilometres, Switzerland about 41,000. 17,000,000 divided by 41,000 gives just over 400.
36000.m: Switzerland fits into Russia over 400 times.

36001.q: Which mountain range in Russia is seen as the border between Europe and Asia?
36001.e: The Urals run from north to south through Russia. Europe lies to the west of them, Asia to the east.
36001.m: The Urals separate Europe and Asia.

36002.q: What is the famous fortress in Moscow where the Russian president has his official seat?
36002.e: The Kremlin is an old fortress in the middle of Moscow with walls, towers and palaces. The president has his official seat there.
36002.m: The president has his official seat in the Moscow Kremlin.

36003.q: Which is the smallest country in the world?
36003.e: Vatican City is smaller than half a square kilometre. No other country is so small.
36003.m: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world.

36004.q: Who is the head of state of Vatican City?
36004.e: The Pope is the head of the Catholic Church. At the same time he is head of state of Vatican City.

36005.q: Which soldiers from Switzerland protect the Pope?
36005.e: The Swiss Guard is a small army of Swiss men. They wear colourful uniforms in blue, yellow and red.
36005.m: The Swiss Guard protects the Pope.

36006.q: Since which year has the Swiss Guard protected the Pope?
36006.e: The first Swiss guards came to Rome in 1506. The Swiss Guard is considered the oldest army in the world still in existence.
36006.m: The Swiss Guard has guarded the Pope since 1506.

36007.q: What is the big church in Vatican City called?
36007.e: St Peter’s Basilica is one of the largest churches in the world. The Pope holds big services there.
36007.m: St Peter’s Basilica stands in the Vatican.

36008.q: Roughly how many people live in Vatican City?
36008.e: Only a few hundred people live in Vatican City, among them clergy and Swiss guards. No country has fewer inhabitants.
36008.m: Fewer than 1,000 people live in Vatican City.

36009.q: What colours is the flag of Vatican City?
36009.e: The flag is yellow on the left and white on the right. The white part shows two crossed keys and the papal crown.
36009.m: The flag of Vatican City is yellow and white.

36010.q: Which two countries share the longest border in the world?
36010.e: The border between the USA and Canada is almost 9,000 kilometres long. A long section runs as a straight line across the land.
36010.m: The USA and Canada share the longest border in the world.

36011.q: What is meant by the “green border”?
a: The border through woods and fields away from crossings
A border that is painted green
36011.e: Between the border crossings, the border runs through woods, meadows and fields. This part is called the green border.
36011.m: The green border lies away from the border crossings.

36012.q: Which wall divided the city of Berlin into two parts until 1989?
36012.e: The Berlin Wall divided Berlin into East and West from 1961 to 1989. In November 1989 it was opened.

36013.q: Who is President of Russia (as of 2026)?
36013.e: Vladimir Putin has been President of Russia since 2000, with one break. From 2008 to 2012 Dmitry Medvedev was president.
36013.m: Vladimir Putin is President of Russia.

36014.q: What do you call a state that has no king but an elected head?
36014.e: In a republic the head of state is elected and serves only for a certain time. Switzerland is a republic too.
36014.m: A republic has an elected head of state.

36015.q: How many members does the Swiss Federal Council have?
36015.e: The Federal Council has seven members. Each one leads a department, for example for finance or transport.
36015.m: The Federal Council has seven members.

36016.q: In which building in Bern do the Federal Council and Parliament work?
36016.e: The Federal Palace stands in Bern high above the River Aare. Parliament and the Federal Council meet there.
36016.m: The Federal Council and Parliament work in the Federal Palace.

36017.q: What is the name of the Pope who has led the Catholic Church since 2025?
36017.e: In May 2025 the cardinals elected Robert Prevost as Pope. He took the name Leo XIV and is the first Pope from the USA.
36017.m: Leo XIV has been Pope since 2025.

36018.q: Which country takes up almost a whole continent?
36018.e: The mainland of Australia belongs entirely to a single state. The island of Tasmania belongs to it too.
36018.m: Australia is a country as big as a continent.

36019.q: What colours is the flag of Germany?
36019.e: The German flag has three horizontal stripes: black at the top, red in the middle and gold at the bottom.
36019.m: The German flag is black, red and gold.

36020.q: In which direction does Germany lie as seen from Switzerland?
36020.e: Germany borders Switzerland to the north, for example the cantons of Basel-Stadt, Aargau and Schaffhausen.

36021.q: Which famous gate stands in Berlin?
36021.e: The Brandenburg Gate is Berlin’s best-known landmark. It is a symbol of German unity.
36021.m: The Brandenburg Gate is the landmark of Berlin.

36022.q: How many federal states is Germany divided into?
36022.e: Germany has 16 federal states, for example Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg. They are a bit like our cantons.
36022.m: Germany is made up of 16 federal states.

36023.q: Which German federal state borders Switzerland?
36023.e: Baden-Württemberg lies directly north of Switzerland. Towns such as Lörrach and Waldshut belong to it.
36023.m: Baden-Württemberg is the German federal state on the Swiss border.

36024.q: Which river forms a large part of the border between Switzerland and Germany?
36024.e: The Rhine flows between Lake Constance and Basel. For many kilometres it separates Switzerland from Germany.
36024.m: The Rhine forms a large part of the border with Germany.

36025.q: What is the German village that is completely surrounded by Switzerland called?
36025.e: Büsingen on the High Rhine belongs to Germany but is surrounded on all sides by Swiss territory. It lies near the canton of Schaffhausen.
36025.m: Büsingen is a German village in the middle of Switzerland.

36026.q: Which of Switzerland’s neighbours has the most inhabitants?
36026.e: More than 80 million people live in Germany. That is almost ten times as many as in Switzerland.
36026.m: Germany is the neighbouring country with the most inhabitants.

36027.q: Which famous tower stands in Paris?
36027.e: The Eiffel Tower was built in 1889 for a world fair. It is made of iron and is now over 300 metres tall.
36027.m: The Eiffel Tower is the landmark of Paris.

36028.q: Which river flows through the middle of Paris?
36028.e: The Seine flows right through Paris. Many beautiful bridges cross it.

36029.q: In which direction does France lie as seen from Switzerland?
36029.e: France lies to the west of Switzerland. For example, the cantons of Geneva, Vaud, Neuchâtel and Jura border France.

36030.q: Which Swiss canton is almost entirely surrounded by France?
36030.e: The canton of Geneva is surrounded by France almost all the way round. Only a small part borders the canton of Vaud.
36030.m: The canton of Geneva is almost entirely surrounded by France.

36031.q: Which mountain range lies on the border between Switzerland and France?
36031.e: The Jura is a long mountain range. It stretches from Geneva to Basel and lies partly in Switzerland and partly in France.
36031.m: The Jura lies on the border with France.

36032.q: Which famous painting hangs in the Louvre in Paris?
36032.e: The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci. It hangs in the Louvre, one of the largest museums in the world.
36032.m: The Mona Lisa hangs in the Louvre in Paris.

36033.q: Which old oval building stands in Rome?
36033.e: The Colosseum is almost 2,000 years old. Gladiators used to fight there.
36033.m: The Colosseum is an old building in Rome.

36034.q: Which Swiss canton borders Italy and speaks Italian?
36034.e: The canton of Ticino lies in the south of Switzerland. People there speak Italian, as in neighbouring Italy.
36034.m: In Ticino people speak Italian, as in Italy.

36035.q: Which small country lies in the middle of the city of Rome?
36035.e: Vatican City is a country of its own in Rome. The Pope lives there, and the Swiss Guard protects him.
36035.m: Vatican City lies in the middle of Rome.

36036.q: Which famous mountain stands on the border between Valais and Italy?
36036.e: The Matterhorn stands right on the border. In Italian it is called Monte Cervino.
36036.m: The Matterhorn stands on the border with Italy.

36037.q: Which lake lies partly in Ticino and partly in Italy?
36037.e: Most of Lake Maggiore lies in Italy. Its northern end with Locarno belongs to Ticino.
36037.m: Lake Maggiore lies in Switzerland and Italy.

36038.q: What colours is the flag of Austria?
a: Red and white with a cross
36038.e: The Austrian flag has three horizontal stripes: red at the top, white in the middle and red again at the bottom.
36038.m: The flag of Austria is red, white and red.

36039.q: In which direction does Austria lie as seen from Switzerland?
36039.e: Austria lies to the east of Switzerland. It borders the cantons of St Gallen and the Grisons.

36040.q: Which language is mainly spoken in Austria?
36040.e: People in Austria speak German. But many words sound different from Swiss German, for example ‘Paradeiser’ for tomato.

36041.q: Which Austrian federal state borders Switzerland?
36041.e: Vorarlberg is Austria’s westernmost federal state and borders the cantons of St Gallen and the Grisons. Tyrol also borders Switzerland.
36041.m: Vorarlberg is an Austrian federal state on the Swiss border.

36042.q: Which big river flows through Vienna?
36042.e: The Danube is one of the longest rivers in Europe. It also flows through Vienna.

36043.q: Which famous palace stands in Vienna?
36043.e: Schönbrunn Palace was the summer palace of the imperial family. Today a great many people visit it every year.

36044.q: In which Austrian city was the musician Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart born?
36044.e: Mozart was born in Salzburg in 1756. You can visit the house where he was born there today.

36045.q: Which famous church stands in the middle of Vienna?
36045.e: St Stephen’s Cathedral is the landmark of Vienna. The people of Vienna affectionately call it ‘Steffl’.
36045.m: St Stephen’s Cathedral is the landmark of Vienna.

36046.q: Between which two countries does Liechtenstein lie?
36046.e: Liechtenstein borders Switzerland to the west and Austria to the east. It borders no other countries.
36046.m: Liechtenstein lies between Switzerland and Austria.

36047.q: What money do people pay with in Liechtenstein?
36047.e: Liechtenstein has no money of its own. For more than 100 years people there have paid with Swiss francs.
36047.m: In Liechtenstein people pay with Swiss francs.

36048.q: Which language is spoken in Liechtenstein?
36048.e: The official language in Liechtenstein is German. In everyday life people speak a dialect that sounds similar to the one in the Rhine Valley.

36049.q: Which river separates Liechtenstein from Switzerland?
36049.e: The Rhine flows through the Rhine Valley. It forms the border between Liechtenstein and the canton of St Gallen.
36049.m: The Rhine separates Liechtenstein from Switzerland.

36050.q: How big is Liechtenstein compared with Switzerland?
36050.e: Liechtenstein is one of the smallest countries in the world. It covers only about 160 square kilometres, less than the canton of Zug.
36050.m: Liechtenstein is a very small country.

36051.q: What does the flag of Liechtenstein look like?
a: Blue and red with a crown
Red and white with a cross
Green and white with a star
Yellow and black with an eagle
36051.e: The flag has a blue stripe at the top and a red one at the bottom. In the top left corner is a golden crown.
36051.m: The flag of Liechtenstein is blue and red with a golden crown.

36052.q: How many municipalities does Liechtenstein have?
36052.e: Liechtenstein has only 11 municipalities, for example Vaduz, Schaan and Balzers.
36052.m: Liechtenstein is made up of 11 municipalities.

36053.q: Who is the head of state of Liechtenstein?
36053.e: Liechtenstein is a principality. The head of state is the prince from the Liechtenstein family.
36053.m: Liechtenstein is led by a prince.

36054.q: What is the name of the Prince of Liechtenstein (as of 2026)?
36054.e: Prince Hans-Adam II has been the head of state of Liechtenstein since 1989.
36054.m: Hans-Adam II is the Prince of Liechtenstein.

36055.q: Where does the princely family of Liechtenstein live?
36055.e: Vaduz Castle stands high above the capital. The princely family lives there, so it cannot be visited.
36055.m: The princely family lives in Vaduz Castle.

36056.q: What is the prince’s son who will be the next prince called?
36056.e: The Hereditary Prince is the heir to the throne. He will later take over the office of prince.
36056.m: The Hereditary Prince will one day become prince.

36057.q: Who has carried out most of the duties for the Prince of Liechtenstein since 2004?
36057.e: In 2004 Prince Hans-Adam II made his son Alois his deputy. Since then Alois has handled most of the official business.
36057.m: Hereditary Prince Alois has represented the prince since 2004.

36058.q: In which month does Liechtenstein celebrate its national day, the same month as Switzerland’s National Day?
36058.e: Liechtenstein celebrates on 15 August, Switzerland on 1 August. On national day the princely family invites the people into the castle garden.
36058.m: Liechtenstein celebrates its national day in August.

36059.q: Where does the country of Liechtenstein get its name from?
36059.e: The country is named after the princely family of Liechtenstein. The family bought the territory about 300 years ago.
36059.m: Liechtenstein is named after its princely family.

36060.q: What do you call a country that is led by a prince?
36060.e: A country with a prince at its head is called a principality. Liechtenstein is a principality.

36061.q: Who is the Chancellor of Germany (as of 2026)?
36061.e: Friedrich Merz has been German Chancellor since May 2025. He belongs to the CDU party.
36061.m: Friedrich Merz has been Chancellor of Germany since 2025.

36062.q: What does the Chancellor do in Germany?
36062.e: The Chancellor is the head of the German government. He decides which direction politics takes.
36062.m: The Chancellor leads the German government.

36063.q: Who was the first woman to be Chancellor of Germany?
36063.e: Angela Merkel was Chancellor from 2005 to 2021. She was the first woman in this office.
36063.m: Angela Merkel was Germany’s first female Chancellor.

36064.q: In which city does the German Chancellor work?
36064.e: The Chancellor works in the Chancellery in Berlin. It stands very close to the Reichstag building.
36064.m: The Chancellor works in the Chancellery in Berlin.

36065.q: Who elects the Chancellor in Germany?
36065.e: The members of the Bundestag elect the Chancellor. Before that, the people elect the members.

36066.q: Who was Chancellor of Germany from 2021 to 2025?
36066.e: Olaf Scholz of the SPD was Chancellor from December 2021 to May 2025.
36066.m: Olaf Scholz was Chancellor from 2021 to 2025.

36067.q: Who was the first Chancellor of Germany?
36067.e: Konrad Adenauer became the first Chancellor in 1949. He stayed in office for 14 years.
36067.m: Konrad Adenauer was the first German Chancellor.

36068.q: In Germany, what is the head of state alongside the Chancellor called?
36068.e: Germany has a Federal President as head of state. But the government is led by the Chancellor.
36068.m: In Germany the Federal President is the head of state.

36069.q: Who leads the government in France on behalf of the President?
36069.e: The President appoints a Prime Minister. This person leads the government.
36069.m: In France the Prime Minister leads the government.

36070.q: In which palace in Paris does the French President work?
36070.e: The Élysée Palace is the official residence of the French President. It is in the middle of Paris.
36070.m: The French President works in the Élysée Palace.

36071.q: Who elects the President in France?
36071.e: In France the citizens elect the President directly. That is different from our Federal Council.
36071.m: In France the people elect the President.

36072.q: For how many years is the French President elected?
36072.e: The President’s term of office lasts 5 years. A person may be elected at most twice in a row.
36072.m: The French President is elected for 5 years.

36073.q: What is the French President for his country?
36073.e: The President is France’s head of state. He has a lot of power and is also the supreme commander of the army.
36073.m: The President is the head of state of France.

36074.q: On which day does France celebrate its national day with a parade?
36074.e: On 14 July there is a big parade in Paris. The President watches it on the Champs-Élysées.
36074.m: France celebrates its national day on 14 July.

36075.q: How many times has Emmanuel Macron been elected President?
36075.e: Macron was elected for the first time in 2017 and for the second time in 2022.
36075.m: Emmanuel Macron has been elected President twice.

36076.q: What is the national anthem played for the French President called?
36076.e: The Marseillaise is the national anthem of France. It is played at the President’s official ceremonies.
36076.m: The national anthem of France is the Marseillaise.

36077.q: Which river flows through Lake Constance?
36077.e: The Rhine flows into Lake Constance in the east, on the border between Switzerland and Austria. At Stein am Rhein it flows out again.
36077.m: The Rhine flows through Lake Constance.

36078.q: Which Swiss canton has the longest shore on Lake Constance?
36078.e: The canton of Thurgau lies on the southern shore of Lake Constance. Places like Romanshorn and Arbon are there.
36078.m: Thurgau has the longest Swiss shore on Lake Constance.

36079.q: What is the flower island in Lake Constance called?
36079.e: The island of Mainau belongs to Germany. It is famous for its many flowers and plants.
36079.m: Mainau is the flower island in Lake Constance.

36080.q: Which Austrian town lies on Lake Constance?
36080.e: Bregenz lies on the eastern shore of Lake Constance. Every summer there is a festival there on a stage in the lake.
36080.m: Bregenz is the Austrian town on Lake Constance.

36081.q: Which German town lies right on the border with Kreuzlingen on Lake Constance?
36081.e: Konstanz and Kreuzlingen have grown together. The border runs right between the two towns.
36081.m: Konstanz lies right next to Kreuzlingen.

36082.q: What is Lake Constance sometimes called because of its size?
36082.e: Lake Constance is so big that you sometimes can hardly see the other shore. That is why it is also called the Swabian Sea.
36082.m: Lake Constance is also called the Swabian Sea.

36083.q: How can you travel from Romanshorn straight across Lake Constance to Friedrichshafen?
36083.e: A ferry runs from Romanshorn in Switzerland to Friedrichshafen in Germany. It also takes cars and bikes.
36083.m: A ferry connects Romanshorn with Friedrichshafen.

a: Someone who works in the neighbouring country
36084.e: A cross-border commuter lives in one country and works in another. They regularly travel across the border.
36084.m: A cross-border commuter lives in one country and works in the neighbouring one.

36085.q: Which permit do cross-border commuters working in Switzerland get?
36085.e: Cross-border commuters receive a cross-border commuter permit, permit G. The G stands for the German word ‘Grenzgänger’.
36085.m: Cross-border commuters in Switzerland have permit G.

36086.q: Which country do most cross-border commuters in Ticino come from?
36086.e: Ticino borders Italy. That is why almost all cross-border commuters there come from Italy.
36086.m: In Ticino most cross-border commuters come from Italy.

36087.q: From which neighbouring country do the most cross-border commuters come to Switzerland overall?
36087.e: More than half of all cross-border commuters in Switzerland live in France. Italy and Germany follow.
36087.m: Most cross-border commuters come to Switzerland from France.

36088.q: Roughly how many cross-border commuters work in Switzerland (as of 2026)?
36088.e: According to the Federal Statistical Office, about 414,000 cross-border commuters were working in Switzerland in summer 2026.
36088.m: About 400,000 cross-border commuters work in Switzerland.

36089.q: When do cross-border commuters normally cross the border?
a: On the way to work and back
36089.e: Cross-border commuters commute. In the morning they travel to work in the neighbouring country and later back home again.
36089.m: Cross-border commuters travel across the border between home and work.

36090.q: In which Swiss canton do the most cross-border commuters work?
36090.e: More cross-border commuters work in the canton of Geneva than in any other canton. Ticino and Vaud follow.
36090.m: The most cross-border commuters work in the canton of Geneva.

36091.q: Why are there often traffic jams in the morning at border crossings near Basel or Geneva?
a: Because many cross-border commuters drive to work
Because cows cross the road there
36091.e: Every morning many cross-border commuters drive to work in Switzerland at the same time. That is why there are often queues at the border crossings.
36091.m: Many cross-border commuters cause traffic at the borders in the morning.

36092.q: Which three countries meet at the Three Countries Corner in Basel?
36092.e: The borders of Switzerland, Germany and France meet in Basel.
36092.m: Switzerland, Germany and France meet in Basel.

36093.q: In which river do the three borders at the Basel Three Countries Corner meet exactly?
36093.e: The exact point where the three borders meet lies in the middle of the Rhine.
36093.m: The tripoint near Basel lies in the middle of the Rhine.

36094.q: What stands on the bank at the Basel Three Countries Corner as a landmark?
36094.e: On the bank of the Rhine in Kleinhüningen stands a tall silver monument. It is close to the spot where the three countries meet.
36094.m: A silver monument marks the Three Countries Corner in Basel.

36095.q: Which bridge connects Germany and France right by the Basel Three Countries Corner?
36095.e: The Three Countries Bridge leads from Weil am Rhein to Huningue. You may only cross it on foot or by bike.
36095.m: The Three Countries Bridge connects Germany and France near Basel.

36096.q: In which country is the airport that serves Basel?
36096.e: The EuroAirport lies on French soil. It is run jointly by France and Switzerland.

36097.q: How can you travel from Basel directly to Weil am Rhein in Germany?
36097.e: Tram line 8 runs from Basel across the border to Weil am Rhein.
36097.m: A Basel tram runs into Germany.

36098.q: Which Basel railway station is run by Deutsche Bahn?
36098.e: The Badischer Bahnhof is in Basel but is run by Deutsche Bahn, the German railway. Many trains to Germany leave from there.
36098.m: The Badischer Bahnhof in Basel belongs to Deutsche Bahn.

36099.q: What is there at the Basel Three Countries Corner where ships arrive?
36099.e: The Rhine port of Kleinhüningen is at the Three Countries Corner. Ships unload goods there that come along the Rhine.
36099.m: There is a Rhine port at the Three Countries Corner in Basel.

36100.q: What money do people pay with in Germany, France, Italy and Austria?
36100.e: These four neighbouring countries all have the euro. Switzerland, on the other hand, has the Swiss franc.
36100.m: Four of Switzerland’s neighbours pay with euros.

36101.q: Which sign stands for the euro?
36101.e: The sign for the euro is €. It looks like an E with two lines.
36101.m: The sign for the euro is €.

36102.q: How many cents make one euro?
36102.e: One euro has 100 cents, just as one franc has 100 centimes.

36103.q: Since which year have there been euro coins and euro notes?
36103.e: On 1 January 2002 the first euro coins and notes went into people’s purses.
36103.m: Euro coins and notes have existed since 2002.

36104.q: What colour are the small euro coins of 1, 2 and 5 cents?
36104.e: The 1, 2 and 5 cent coins are made of steel with a layer of copper. That is why they shine reddish.
36104.m: The small cent coins are copper red.

36105.q: Who is shown on the Austrian 1 euro coin?
36105.e: Each euro country designs one side of the coins itself. Austria shows the musician Mozart on the 1 euro coin.
36105.m: Mozart is shown on the Austrian 1 euro coin.

36106.q: Which animal can be seen on the German 1 euro and 2 euro coins?
36106.e: The German 1 euro and 2 euro coins show the federal eagle. It is Germany’s heraldic animal.
36106.m: There is an eagle on the German euro coins.

36107.q: What is the smallest euro note?
36107.e: The smallest euro note is worth 5 euros. It is grey.
36107.m: The smallest euro note is worth 5 euros.

36108.q: Who is at the head of the country in a monarchy?
36108.e: In a monarchy a king, a queen or a prince is the head of state. The office is usually passed down within the family.
36108.m: A monarchy has a king, a queen or a prince at its head.

36109.e: Switzerland is a republic. The people elect the parliament and can vote themselves on many questions.
36109.m: Switzerland has no king, because it is a republic.

36110.q: What do you call a country that is ruled by a king?
36110.e: A country with a king or a queen is called a kingdom. Examples are Spain or Denmark.
36110.m: A country with a king is called a kingdom.

36111.q: How do people usually become king or queen?
a: They are born into the family
36111.e: In a monarchy a child of the king or queen usually inherits the office. That is why it is called a hereditary monarchy.
36111.m: People usually become king or queen because their parents ruled before them.

36112.q: How do you address a king politely?
36112.e: Kings and queens are addressed as “Majesty”. It is an old and very polite form of address.
36112.m: You address a king as “Your Majesty”.

36113.q: How long does a king usually stay in office?
36113.e: A king usually reigns for his whole life. But some kings give up the office voluntarily when they are old.
36113.m: A king usually reigns until the end of his life.

36114.q: Who makes the laws in Great Britain today?
36114.e: Great Britain is a parliamentary monarchy. The king has little power; Parliament passes the laws.
36114.m: In Great Britain Parliament passes the laws, not the king.

36115.q: What is the wife of a king called?
36115.e: When a man is king, his wife is usually called queen. A king and his wife are the royal couple.
36115.m: The wife of a king is called queen.

36116.q: Where does a king wear his crown?
36116.e: A crown is a piece of jewellery that you put on your head. It shows everyone: this is the king or the queen.
36116.m: A king wears the crown on his head.

36117.q: What metal are royal crowns usually made of?
36117.e: Royal crowns are usually made of gold or silver. These metals shine beautifully and are valuable.
36117.m: Royal crowns are usually made of gold.

36118.q: What often sparkles on a crown?
36118.e: Valuable gems such as diamonds, rubies and sapphires shine on crowns. That is why crowns are very valuable.
36118.m: Valuable precious stones sparkle on a real crown.

36119.q: Where are the British Crown Jewels kept?
36119.e: The Crown Jewels are kept well guarded in the Tower of London, an old castle on the Thames. Visitors can look at them there.
36119.m: The British Crown Jewels are in the Tower of London.

36120.e: The crown is a symbol of power. Whoever wears it is a king, queen or emperor.
36120.m: The crown is a symbol of a ruler’s power.

36121.q: What shape does a crown usually have?
36121.e: A crown is usually a circlet, in other words a ring, with points or arches. That way it fits on the head.
36121.m: A crown is usually a ring with points.

36122.q: Where does a king hold his sceptre?
36122.e: At big ceremonies the king holds the sceptre in his hand. That way everyone sees that he rules.
36122.m: A king holds his sceptre in his hand.

36123.q: What is the golden ball with a cross that a king holds in his hand called?
36123.e: The orb is a golden ball with a cross on top. Along with the crown and sceptre, it is one of a ruler’s symbols.
36123.m: The golden ball with a cross is called an orb.

36124.q: Which large gemstone is set in the British Sceptre with the Cross?
36124.e: The Sceptre with the Cross holds the diamond “Cullinan I”. It is one of the largest cut diamonds in the world.
36124.m: A huge diamond sparkles in the British sceptre.

36125.q: Which bird sits on top of a British coronation sceptre?
36125.e: At the coronation the king also holds a sceptre with a white dove. The dove is a symbol of peace and the Holy Spirit.
36125.m: A white dove sits on a British sceptre.

36126.e: A throne is a particularly splendid chair. The king or queen sits on it on ceremonial occasions.
36126.m: A throne is a king’s splendid seat.

36127.q: What does “to ascend the throne” mean?
36127.e: Anyone who ascends the throne becomes the new king or queen. They don’t really climb onto the chair.
36127.m: Whoever ascends the throne becomes king or queen.

36128.q: How is a throne usually decorated?
36128.e: Thrones are often gilded and padded with soft red velvet. They are meant to look splendid and valuable.
36128.m: A throne is often decorated with gold and velvet.

36129.q: Why does a throne often stand on a few steps?
a: So it is easier to clean
36129.e: The throne often stands raised on steps. That way the king sits above everyone else and everyone can see him well.
36129.m: A throne stands raised so the king sits above everyone.

36130.q: Roughly how old is the Coronation Chair in London?
36130.e: The Coronation Chair was made around the year 1300. British kings are crowned on it.
36130.m: The Coronation Chair in London is about 700 years old.

36131.q: What material is the old Coronation Chair in London made of?
36131.e: The Coronation Chair is made of oak. It used to be painted with gold.
36131.m: The old Coronation Chair in London is made of wood.

a: Someone has a crown placed on their head
36132.e: At a coronation a crown is ceremonially placed on the head of a new king or queen. After that they are officially crowned.
36132.m: At a coronation the new ruler has the crown placed on their head.

36133.q: In which church are British kings crowned?
36133.e: For almost 1,000 years British coronations have taken place in Westminster Abbey in London. It is a big old church.
36133.m: British kings are crowned in Westminster Abbey.

36134.q: In which year was King Charles III crowned?
36134.e: King Charles III was crowned in London on 6 May 2023. The ceremony lasted several hours.

36135.q: Who places the crown on the British king’s head at the coronation?
a: The captain of the football team
36135.e: The Archbishop of Canterbury is the senior clergyman of the Church of England. By tradition he crowns the king.
36135.m: The Archbishop of Canterbury places the crown on the British king’s head.

36136.q: How does the British king travel to his coronation?
36136.e: The king travels to the coronation in a splendid carriage pulled by horses. Many people cheer at the roadside.
36136.m: The British king travels to the coronation in a horse-drawn carriage.

36137.q: What does the royal family do after the coronation?
36137.e: After the coronation the royal family appears on the balcony of Buckingham Palace. Many people stand below and cheer.
36137.m: After the coronation the royal family waves from the balcony.

36138.q: Which British coronation was the first to be shown almost entirely on television?
36138.e: The coronation of Queen Elizabeth II on 2 June 1953 was broadcast on television. Millions of people watched.
36138.m: The coronation of Elizabeth II was broadcast on television.

36139.q: In which country does the British royal family live?
36139.e: The British royal family lives in the United Kingdom. It is made up of England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.
36139.m: The British royal family lives in the United Kingdom.

36140.q: What is the name of Prince William’s wife?
36140.e: Prince William married Catherine Middleton in 2011. Many people simply call her Kate.
36140.m: Prince William is married to Catherine.

36141.q: How many children do Prince William and Catherine have?
36141.e: William and Catherine have two sons and a daughter.
36141.m: William and Catherine have three children.

36142.q: What is the name of Prince William’s brother?
36142.e: Prince Harry is Prince William’s younger brother. He was born in 1984.
36142.m: Prince William’s brother is called Harry.

36143.q: What was the name of the mother of Prince William and Prince Harry?
36143.e: Princess Diana was Charles’s first wife. She was very popular with many people.
36143.m: William and Harry’s mother was called Diana.

36144.q: What is the name of Prince Harry’s wife?
36144.e: In 2018 Prince Harry married the American actress Meghan Markle. The two of them have two children.
36144.m: Prince Harry is married to Meghan.

36145.q: What was the name of Queen Elizabeth II’s husband?
36145.e: Prince Philip was married to Elizabeth II for more than 70 years. He died in 2021 aged 99.
36145.m: Elizabeth II’s husband was called Prince Philip.

36146.q: What is the name of King Charles III’s only sister?
36146.e: Princess Anne is the only daughter of Elizabeth II. She was born in 1950, almost two years after Charles.
36146.m: King Charles III’s sister is called Anne.

36147.q: Who has been King of the United Kingdom since 2022?
36147.e: Charles III became king on 8 September 2022, when his mother died. Before that he was heir to the throne for a very long time.
36147.m: Charles III has been King of the United Kingdom since 2022.

36148.q: Who was King Charles III’s mother?
36148.e: Charles is the eldest son of Queen Elizabeth II. That is why he became king after her.
36148.m: King Charles III’s mother was Queen Elizabeth II.

36149.q: What is the name of King Charles III’s wife?
36149.e: Charles married Camilla in 2005. Since he became king she has been Queen Camilla.
36149.m: King Charles III is married to Queen Camilla.

36150.q: What has King Charles III supported for many years?
36150.e: Charles loves gardens and has long campaigned for the protection of nature. He often talks about the environment and climate.
36150.m: King Charles III supports nature and the environment.

36151.q: How many sons does King Charles III have?
36151.e: Charles has two sons from his first marriage. The elder will one day be king.
36151.m: King Charles III has two sons.

36152.q: In which year was Charles III born?
36152.e: Charles was born in London on 14 November 1948. He was already over 70 when he became king.
36152.m: King Charles III was born in 1948.

36153.q: Apart from Great Britain, where else is Charles III king?
36153.e: Charles III is also King of Canada, Australia, New Zealand and several other countries. These countries belong to the Commonwealth.
36153.m: Charles III is also King of Canada and Australia.

36154.q: Which title did Charles hold before he became king?
36154.e: Charles held the title Prince of Wales for over 60 years, longer than anyone before him.
36154.m: Before he became king, Charles was Prince of Wales.

36155.q: How long was Elizabeth II queen?
36155.e: Elizabeth II became queen in 1952 and reigned until her death. No British queen or king has reigned longer.
36155.m: Elizabeth II was queen for about 70 years.

36156.q: Which dogs did Queen Elizabeth II particularly love?
36156.e: Elizabeth II had many corgis in her life. They are small dogs with short legs and big ears.

36157.q: How old was Queen Elizabeth II when she died?
36157.e: Elizabeth II died aged 96 at Balmoral Castle in Scotland. She was queen until the very end.

36158.q: How many children did Queen Elizabeth II have?
36158.e: Elizabeth II had three sons and one daughter.
36158.m: Queen Elizabeth II had four children.

36159.q: Which animal did Elizabeth II like to ride until old age?
36159.e: Elizabeth II loved horses. She was still riding when she was over 90 and also owned racehorses.
36159.m: Queen Elizabeth II loved riding horses.

36160.q: How old was Elizabeth when she became queen in 1952?
36160.e: Elizabeth was born in 1926 and became queen in 1952 when her father died. She was 25 years old at the time.
36160.m: Elizabeth became queen at the age of 25.

36161.q: What was the big celebration in 2022 for Elizabeth II’s years on the throne called?
36161.e: In 2022 Great Britain celebrated the Queen’s Platinum Jubilee. For four days there were parades and parties.
36161.m: Elizabeth II’s big jubilee in 2022 was called the Platinum Jubilee.

36162.q: Who was the father of Elizabeth II?
36162.e: Elizabeth was the elder daughter of King George VI. After his death in 1952 she became queen.
36162.m: Elizabeth II’s father was King George VI.

36163.q: What do you call the son of a king?
36163.e: The son of a king or queen is a prince. He belongs to the royal family.
36163.m: The son of a king is a prince.

36164.q: Which prince holds the title “Prince of Wales” today?
36164.e: Since 2022 Prince William has been the Prince of Wales. He is the eldest son of King Charles III.
36164.m: Prince William is the Prince of Wales today.

36165.q: What is the name of Prince William’s eldest son?
36165.e: Prince George was born in London in 2013.
36165.m: Prince William’s eldest son is called George.

36166.q: What is the name of Prince William’s youngest son?
36166.e: Prince Louis was born in 2018 as the youngest child of William and Catherine.
36166.m: Prince William’s youngest son is called Louis.

36167.q: What do you call a prince who is meant to become king later?
36167.e: The crown prince is the prince who will be the next king. He will later wear the crown.
36167.m: A crown prince is meant to become king later.

36168.q: In which country does Prince Harry live with his family today?
36168.e: In 2020 Prince Harry moved with his family to California in the USA. He no longer works for the royal family.
36168.m: Prince Harry lives in the USA today.

36169.q: What is the husband of a queen who is not king himself called?
36169.e: The husband of a reigning queen is often called prince consort. He helps her but does not rule himself.
36169.m: The husband of a queen is often called prince consort.

36170.q: What do you call the daughter of a king?
36170.e: The daughter of a king or queen is a princess. She belongs to the royal family.
36170.m: The daughter of a king is a princess.

36171.q: What is the name of the daughter of Prince William and Catherine?
36171.e: Princess Charlotte was born in London in 2015.
36171.m: Prince William’s daughter is called Charlotte.

36172.q: Which princess died in an accident in Paris in 1997?
36172.e: Princess Diana died in a car accident in Paris in 1997. Many people all over the world mourned her.

36173.e: Princess Anne is the only daughter of Queen Elizabeth II. King Charles III is her older brother.
36173.m: Princess Anne is the daughter of Queen Elizabeth II.

36174.q: Which sport was Princess Anne very successful at?
36174.e: Princess Anne was a very good rider. She even took part in the Olympic Games in 1976.
36174.m: Princess Anne was a successful rider.

36175.q: What is the name of Prince Harry’s older brother?
36175.e: Prince William is Harry’s older brother. He is the heir to the British throne.
36175.m: Prince Harry’s older brother is called William.

36176.q: What is the wife of a prince often called?
36176.e: When a prince marries, his wife is often called princess as well. If the prince later becomes king, she is called queen.
36176.m: The wife of a prince is often called princess.

36177.q: What is an heir to the throne?
a: The person who will be the next king
The person who cleans the throne
The person who carries the throne
The person who builds the throne
36177.e: The heir to the throne becomes king or queen when the current ruler dies or abdicates.
36177.m: An heir to the throne will be the next king.

36178.q: Who is currently first in line to the British throne (as of 2026)?
36178.e: Prince William is the eldest son of King Charles III. That is why he will be the next king.
36178.m: Prince William will be the next British king.

36179.q: Who comes directly after Prince William in the line of succession to the British throne (as of 2026)?
36179.e: After William come his own children first, starting with the eldest.
36179.m: Prince George is directly behind his father in the line of succession.

36180.q: Who usually becomes heir to the throne in a monarchy?
36180.e: In most royal houses the eldest child inherits the throne. After that come that child’s children.
36180.m: The king’s eldest child usually becomes heir to the throne.

36181.q: What applies to girls in the British line of succession today?
a: They have the same rights as boys
36181.e: Younger brothers used to come before older sisters. Since a new rule in 2013, only age counts, whether girl or boy.
36181.m: Today girls and boys have the same rights in the British line of succession.

36182.q: What does a king who abdicates do?
a: He gives up the throne voluntarily
36182.e: To abdicate means that a king stops of his own free will. Then the heir to the throne becomes the new king.
36182.m: Whoever abdicates gives up the throne voluntarily.

36183.q: Queen Margrethe II of Denmark abdicated in January 2024. What does that mean?
a: She gave up the throne voluntarily
36183.e: Whoever abdicates gives up the throne voluntarily. Margrethe II handed it over to her eldest son, who is now king.
36183.m: Whoever abdicates gives up the throne voluntarily.

36184.q: In which city is Buckingham Palace?
36184.e: Buckingham Palace stands in the middle of London. It is the official residence of the British king.

36185.q: Roughly how many rooms does Buckingham Palace have?
36185.e: Buckingham Palace has about 775 rooms, including 19 state rooms and 78 bathrooms. It is huge.

36186.q: What hat do the guards outside Buckingham Palace wear?
36186.e: The guards wear tall black caps made of bearskin. They are known all over the world.
36186.m: The guards at Buckingham Palace wear tall bearskins.

36187.q: What happens at the Changing of the Guard outside Buckingham Palace?
a: The king goes out in his carriage
36187.e: At the Changing of the Guard new soldiers take over the watch. It happens with music and marching, and many tourists watch.
36187.m: At the Changing of the Guard new guards take over duty.

36188.q: What colour are the jackets of the guards outside Buckingham Palace?
36188.e: In summer the guards wear red tunics, in winter grey greatcoats. The black caps go with them.
36188.m: The guards at Buckingham Palace wear red jackets.

36189.q: How can you tell that the king is in Buckingham Palace?
36189.e: When the king is in the palace, the Royal Standard flies on the roof. It is his personal flag.
36189.m: A special flag shows that the king is in the palace.

36190.e: Behind the palace there is a large garden with a lake. Garden parties are held there in summer.
36190.m: A large garden lies behind Buckingham Palace.

36191.q: Which of Switzerland’s neighbouring countries has a prince?
36191.e: Liechtenstein is a small principality between Switzerland and Austria. A prince rules there.
36191.m: Our neighbour Liechtenstein has a prince.

36192.q: What is the name of the King of Spain (as of 2026)?
36192.e: Felipe VI has been King of Spain since 2014. He succeeded his father Juan Carlos.
36192.m: The King of Spain is called Felipe VI.

36193.q: What colour do people in the Netherlands wear on King’s Day?
36193.e: The Dutch royal family is the House of Orange. That is why many people wear orange clothes on King’s Day.
36193.m: On King’s Day the Dutch wear orange.

36194.q: Which of these countries is a kingdom?
36194.e: Sweden has a king, Carl XVI Gustaf. Germany, Italy and Austria are republics.
36194.m: Sweden is a kingdom with a king.

36195.q: Who has been King of Denmark since 2024?
36195.e: Frederik X became King of Denmark in January 2024. He succeeded his mother.
36195.m: Frederik X has been King of Denmark since 2024.

36196.q: Who has been King of Norway since August 2026?
36196.e: King Harald V died in August 2026. His son Haakon became the new king and is now called Haakon VIII.
36196.m: Haakon VIII has been King of Norway since 2026.

36197.q: What is the name of the King of Belgium (as of 2026)?
36197.e: Philippe has been King of the Belgians since 2013. Belgium lies between France and the Netherlands.
36197.m: The King of Belgium is called Philippe.

36198.q: In which country is Willem-Alexander king (as of 2026)?
36198.e: Willem-Alexander has been King of the Netherlands since 2013. He lives in The Hague.
36198.m: Willem-Alexander is King of the Netherlands.

36199.e: Monaco is a principality. A prince is at the head of the country.

36200.q: What is the name of the Prince of Monaco (as of 2026)?
36200.e: Albert II has been Prince of Monaco since 2005. He succeeded his father Rainier III.
36200.m: The Prince of Monaco is called Albert II.

36201.e: Monaco lies on the coast of the Mediterranean. It is warm and sunny there in summer.

36202.q: Which country surrounds Monaco on the land side?
36202.e: On the land side Monaco borders only France. On the other side is the sea.
36202.m: Monaco is surrounded by France on the land side.

36203.q: How big is Monaco compared with other countries?
a: One of the smallest countries in the world
One of the largest countries in the world
36203.e: Monaco is only about 2 square kilometres in size. Only Vatican City is smaller.
36203.m: Monaco is one of the smallest countries in the world.

36204.q: Which famous motor race takes place in Monaco every year?
36204.e: At the Monaco Grand Prix, Formula 1 cars race right through the narrow streets of the city.
36204.m: In Monaco Formula 1 races through the streets.

36205.q: What is the name of Monaco’s princely family?
36205.e: The Grimaldi family has ruled Monaco for more than 700 years.
36205.m: Monaco’s princely family is called Grimaldi.

36206.q: Which language is mainly spoken in Monaco?
36206.e: The official language of Monaco is French. There is also the old language Monégasque.
36206.m: In Monaco people mainly speak French.

36207.q: What is the head of state called in many republics?
36207.e: A republic has no king. The head of state is often a president.
36207.m: In many republics a president is the head of state.

36208.q: Who elects the President of the Swiss Confederation?
36208.e: The United Federal Assembly, in other words the parliament in Bern, elects the President of the Confederation in December.

36209.q: How long is the Swiss President’s term of office?
36209.e: In Switzerland the office changes every year. Then another member of the Federal Council takes over.
36209.m: The Swiss President is in office for only one year.

36210.q: Which group does the Swiss President come from?
36210.e: The President is one of the seven members of the Federal Council. He or she chairs the Federal Council’s meetings.
36210.m: The President is a member of the Federal Council.

36211.q: Who was the first President of the USA?
36211.e: George Washington became the first President of the United States in 1789. The capital of the USA is named after him.
36211.m: George Washington was the first President of the USA.

36212.q: Who is President of the USA (as of 2026)?
36212.e: Donald Trump has been President of the USA again since January 2025. He was already in office from 2017 to 2021.
36212.m: Donald Trump is President of the USA in 2026.

36213.q: Which US president is known for his tall hat and his beard?
36213.e: Abraham Lincoln was president from 1861 to 1865. He often wore a tall top hat and a beard on his chin.
36213.m: Abraham Lincoln wore a tall hat and a beard.

36214.q: How many presidents’ heads are carved into the rock at Mount Rushmore?
36214.e: At Mount Rushmore in South Dakota (USA), the huge heads of four presidents are carved into the rock.
36214.m: Mount Rushmore shows four presidents’ heads in stone.

36215.q: Who was the first Black President of the USA?
36215.e: Barack Obama was president from 2009 to 2017. He was the first African American in this office.
36215.m: Barack Obama was the first Black President of the USA.

36216.q: Who is President of the Swiss Confederation in 2026?
36216.e: In December 2025 Parliament elected Guy Parmelin as President for 2026. He was already President in 2021.
36216.m: Guy Parmelin is President of Switzerland in 2026.

36217.q: In which city is the White House?
36217.e: The White House is in Washington D.C., the capital of the USA.
36217.m: The White House is in the capital, Washington.

36218.q: Who lives and works in the White House?
36218.e: The White House is the official residence and home of the American president and his family.
36218.m: The President of the USA lives in the White House.

36219.q: What shape is the US president’s famous office in the White House?
36219.e: The office is called the “Oval Office” because the room is oval, in other words shaped like an egg.
36219.m: The US president works in an oval office.

36221.q: Which game do children play at Easter in the White House garden?
36221.e: The “Easter Egg Roll” has taken place since 1878. Children roll eggs across the lawn with a spoon.
36221.m: At Easter children roll eggs in the White House garden.

36222.q: Which animal does the US president pardon every year before Thanksgiving?
36222.e: Many Americans eat turkey at Thanksgiving. At a ceremony the president spares the life of one turkey.
36222.m: The US president pardons a turkey every year.

36223.q: What is the president’s wife called in the USA?
36223.e: The president’s wife is called the “First Lady”.
36223.m: The US president’s wife is called the First Lady.

36224.q: Roughly how many rooms does the White House have?
36224.e: The White House has 132 rooms, plus many bathrooms, staircases and fireplaces.
36224.m: The White House has over a hundred rooms.

36225.q: What happened to the White House in 1814?
36225.e: During the war against the USA, British soldiers set fire to the building in 1814. Afterwards it was rebuilt.

36226.q: In which city is the Élysée Palace?
36226.e: The Élysée Palace is in the middle of Paris, the capital of France.
36226.m: The Élysée Palace is in Paris.

36227.q: Who has his official seat in the Élysée Palace?
36227.e: The Élysée Palace is the official seat of the French president. He works there and receives guests.
36227.m: The President of France works in the Élysée Palace.

36228.q: Who is President of France (as of 2026)?
36228.e: Emmanuel Macron has been President of France since 2017. He has been elected twice.
36228.m: Emmanuel Macron is President of France in 2026.

36229.q: Which famous grand avenue is near the Élysée Palace?
36229.e: The palace and the Avenue des Champs-Élysées are close together and have almost the same name.
36229.m: The Champs-Élysées is near the Élysée Palace.

36230.q: What colours is the flag on the Élysée Palace?
36230.e: The French flag flies on the palace. It has three stripes in blue, white and red.
36230.m: The flag of France is blue, white and red.

36231.q: In which country is the Élysée Palace?
36231.e: The Élysée Palace is in Paris, the capital of France. The French president works there.
36231.m: The Élysée Palace is in France.

36232.q: How many years does the French president’s term of office last?
36232.e: Since 2002 the French president has been elected for five years. Before that it was seven years.
36232.m: The President of France is elected for five years.

36233.q: How do you say “President of the Republic” in French?
36233.e: The official title of the French head of state is “président de la République”.
36233.m: In French the office is called président de la République.

36234.q: Who works in the Federal Chancellery in Berlin?
36234.e: The Federal Chancellery is where the German Chancellor and his staff work. The Federal President works in Bellevue Palace.
36234.m: The Chancellor works in the Federal Chancellery.

36235.q: How big is the Federal Chancellery in Berlin compared with the White House?
36235.e: The Federal Chancellery is a huge building. It is about eight times as big as the White House in Washington.
36235.m: The Federal Chancellery is much bigger than the White House.

36236.q: Which funny nickname does the Federal Chancellery have, among others?
36236.e: The building has large round windows in a pale wall. That is why some Berliners call it the “washing machine”.
36236.m: Some Berliners call the Chancellery the washing machine.

36237.q: Which river is the Federal Chancellery on?
36237.e: The Spree flows right through Berlin. The Chancellery stands directly on its bank.
36237.m: The Chancellery stands on the Spree.

36238.q: Which building with a glass dome stands near the Federal Chancellery?
36238.e: The Bundestag meets in the Reichstag building with its glass dome. It is only a few steps from the Chancellery.
36238.m: The Reichstag with its glass dome stands next to the Chancellery.

36239.q: Who became German Chancellor in May 2025?
36239.e: The Bundestag elected Friedrich Merz as Chancellor on 6 May 2025.

36240.q: In which of Switzerland’s neighbouring countries is the head of government also called Federal Chancellor?
36240.e: Austria also has a Federal Chancellor. His Chancellery is in Vienna on the Ballhausplatz.
36240.m: Austria is also governed by a Federal Chancellor.

36241.q: For how many years was Angela Merkel Chancellor?
36241.e: Angela Merkel governed from 2005 to 2021, in other words for 16 years. She was the first woman in this office.
36241.m: Angela Merkel was Chancellor for 16 years.

36242.q: Who leads the government in Great Britain?
36242.e: The king is head of state, but the government is led by the Prime Minister.
36242.m: In Great Britain the Prime Minister leads the government.

36243.q: Who was the first female Prime Minister of Great Britain?
36243.e: Margaret Thatcher became the first woman in this office in 1979. She was called the “Iron Lady”.
36243.m: Margaret Thatcher was the first female British Prime Minister.

36244.q: Which British Prime Minister is famous for his role in the Second World War?
36244.e: Winston Churchill led Great Britain through the Second World War from 1940.
36244.m: Winston Churchill led Great Britain in the Second World War.

36245.q: Who officially appoints the Prime Minister in Great Britain?
36245.e: After an election the monarch invites the person who can form a government and appoints them Prime Minister.
36245.m: The British king appoints the Prime Minister.

36246.q: In which part of the British Parliament does the Prime Minister sit?
36246.e: The Prime Minister is a member of the House of Commons.
36246.m: The British Prime Minister sits in the House of Commons.

36247.q: In which country does a prime minister lead the government?
36247.e: Canada has a prime minister. The USA and Mexico have a president, Switzerland has the Federal Council.
36247.m: Canada is also governed by a prime minister.

36248.q: At which address in London does the British Prime Minister live and work?
36248.e: The house at number 10 Downing Street is the Prime Minister’s official residence. The king, on the other hand, lives in Buckingham Palace.
36248.m: The British Prime Minister lives at 10 Downing Street.

36249.q: Which British Prime Minister was in office for only about 50 days in 2022?
36249.e: Liz Truss was Prime Minister for only 49 days. That is the shortest term of office in Great Britain.
36249.m: Liz Truss was the Prime Minister with the shortest term of office.

36250.q: In which city is 10 Downing Street?
36250.e: Downing Street is a small street in London, close to Parliament.

36251.e: The house is the official residence and home of the British Prime Minister.
36251.m: The British Prime Minister lives at 10 Downing Street.

36252.q: What colour is the famous front door of 10 Downing Street?
36252.e: The front door is black and has a white number 10 on it.
36252.m: The door of 10 Downing Street is black.

36253.q: What is the name of the cat that catches mice at 10 Downing Street?
36253.e: Larry the cat has lived there since 2011 and holds the title “Chief Mouser”.
36253.m: Larry the cat is the mouser at 10 Downing Street.

36254.q: Who lives and works at 10 Downing Street in London?
36254.e: 10 Downing Street is the official residence of the British Prime Minister. The head of government works and lives there.
36254.m: The British Prime Minister lives at 10 Downing Street.

36255.q: What is missing on the outside of the door of 10 Downing Street?
36255.e: The door has no keyhole on the outside. It is always opened from the inside, because someone is always there.
36255.m: The door of 10 Downing Street has no keyhole on the outside.

36256.q: What do the British often call 10 Downing Street for short?
36256.e: Many British people simply say “Number Ten”. They mean the Prime Minister’s official residence.
36256.m: 10 Downing Street is called Number Ten for short.

36257.q: Which animal can be seen as the door knocker on the door of 10 Downing Street?
36257.e: On the black door hangs a door knocker with a lion’s head.
36257.m: The door knocker of 10 Downing Street has a lion’s head.

36258.q: What is an oath of office?
36258.e: Anyone who starts an important office promises solemnly to carry out their duties well and to respect the constitution.
36258.m: An oath of office is a solemn promise made at the start of an office.

36259.q: On which book do many US presidents place their hand when taking the oath of office?
36259.e: Many presidents place their left hand on a Bible. But it is not required.
36259.m: Many US presidents swear with their hand on the Bible.

36260.q: On which day does a new US president take the oath of office?
36260.e: The term of office begins on 20 January after the election. On this day the new president is sworn in.
36260.m: The US president is sworn in on 20 January.

36261.q: Where is the US president usually sworn in?
36261.e: The ceremony usually takes place outdoors in front of the Capitol in Washington. In 2025 it was so cold that it was held inside the Capitol.
36261.m: The US president is usually sworn in outside the Capitol.

36262.q: Who normally administers the oath of office to the US president?
36262.e: The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court says the oath first. The president repeats it.
36262.m: The Chief Justice of the USA administers the oath of office.

36263.q: What may new Swiss federal councillors make instead of an oath?
36263.e: An oath calls upon God, a solemn promise does not. Each person may choose for themselves.
36263.m: In Switzerland you can make a solemn promise instead of an oath.

36264.q: How many fingers do you raise in Switzerland when swearing an oath?
36264.e: You raise your right hand with the thumb, index finger and middle finger. That is three fingers.
36264.m: In Switzerland you raise three fingers when swearing an oath.

36265.q: What does a newly elected member of the Federal Council do before taking office?
a: Takes an oath or makes a solemn promise
36265.e: New federal councillors take an oath or make a solemn promise in front of the Federal Assembly. In this way they promise to respect the constitution and the laws.
36265.m: Anyone taking up a high office takes an oath.

a: An official visit to another country
36266.e: On a state visit a head of state travels officially to another country and is welcomed there with ceremony.
36266.m: On a state visit a head of state travels officially to another country.

36267.q: What is often held in the evening during a state visit?
36267.e: In the evening the host often gives a state banquet. That is a formal festive dinner.
36267.m: There is often a banquet during a state visit.

36268.q: Which music is played when a state guest is welcomed?
36268.e: A military band plays the national anthems of both countries. It is a sign of respect.
36268.m: The national anthems are played during a state visit.

36269.q: Who stands ready in a line when a state guest is welcomed?
36269.e: Soldiers in uniform stand ready as a guard of honour. The guest inspects the line with the host.
36269.m: A guard of honour welcomes the state guest.

36270.q: What do guest and host often exchange during a state visit?
36270.e: Guest and host give each other gifts. They are often typical things from their own country.
36270.m: During a state visit people give each other gifts.

36272.q: In which city does the Federal Council usually receive state guests?
36272.e: The Federal Council usually receives state guests in Bern, for example in the Federal Palace or at the Lohn country residence near Bern.
36272.m: The Federal Council usually receives state guests in Bern.

36273.q: What do state guests often lay at a memorial?
36273.e: With a wreath of flowers the guests honour, for example, people who died for their country.
36273.m: State guests often lay a wreath at a memorial.

36274.q: Who is the red carpet rolled out for?
36274.e: A red carpet shows that a guest is particularly important and is being honoured.
36274.m: The red carpet is rolled out for guests of honour.

36275.q: What colour is the carpet at the Zurich Film Festival?
36275.e: Instead of a red carpet, the Zurich Film Festival has a green one. Green is the festival’s colour.
36275.m: At the Zurich Film Festival people walk on a green carpet.

36276.q: At which awards ceremony in Los Angeles is there a famous red carpet?
36276.e: Before the Oscars ceremony film stars walk along a long red carpet in Los Angeles.
36276.m: There is a famous red carpet at the Oscars.

36277.q: Which country does the oldest known story with a red carpet come from?
36277.e: In the ancient Greek play “Agamemnon”, a red carpet is already laid out for a king.
36277.m: The red carpet already existed in ancient Greece.

36278.q: Where is a red carpet laid out when a state guest arrives by plane?
36278.e: The guest walks down the steps and goes straight along the red carpet to the hosts.
36278.m: The red carpet is laid at the aircraft steps.

36279.q: What does “to roll out the red carpet for someone” mean?
36279.e: The saying means that you honour a guest greatly and welcome them warmly.
36279.m: Whoever rolls out the red carpet welcomes someone especially warmly.

36280.q: What does the red carpet lead up at the Cannes Film Festival?
36280.e: In Cannes the red carpet lies on the steps up to the festival palace. The stars walk up the stairs.
36280.m: In Cannes the red carpet leads up a staircase.

36281.q: Who walks along the red carpet at film premieres?
36281.e: At a film premiere the actors show themselves to the photographers on the red carpet.
36281.m: Actors walk along the red carpet at film premieres.

36282.q: Every how many years does the USA elect a president?
36282.e: A US president’s term of office lasts four years. Then there is another election.
36282.m: The USA elects a president every four years.

36283.q: On which day of the week does the presidential election take place in the USA?
36283.e: Elections in the USA are always held on a Tuesday. This has been fixed since the 19th century.
36283.m: The US presidential election is on a Tuesday.

36284.q: In which month is the president elected in the USA?
36284.e: The election takes place in November. The term of office begins the following January.
36284.m: The USA elects the president in November.

36285.q: Which animal is the symbol of the Republican Party in the USA?
36285.e: The Republicans have an elephant as their symbol, the Democrats a donkey.
36285.m: The elephant is the symbol of the Republicans.

36286.q: What is the maximum number of times someone can be elected President of the USA?
36286.e: Since 1951 an amendment to the constitution has allowed a person to be elected president at most twice.
36286.m: You can be elected US president at most twice.

36287.q: What is the minimum age to become President of the USA?
36287.e: The US constitution requires a minimum age of 35.
36287.m: You can only become US president at 35.

36288.q: Which two big parties compete for the presidency in the USA?
36288.e: There are two big parties in the USA: the Democrats and the Republicans. Almost all presidents came from one of these two.
36288.m: In the USA Democrats and Republicans compete for the presidency.

36289.q: In which year is the next presidential election in the USA (as of 2026)?
36289.e: The last presidential election was in 2024. The next one takes place in 2028.
36289.m: The next US presidential election is in 2028.

36290.q: Who becomes president in the USA if the president dies?
36290.e: The vice-president takes over the office at once if the president dies or resigns.
36290.m: If the US president dies, the vice-president takes over.

36291.q: Who is Vice-President of the USA (as of 2026)?
36291.e: JD Vance has been Vice-President of the USA since January 2025. He works closely with President Donald Trump.
36291.m: JD Vance is Vice-President of the USA in 2026.

36292.q: Which chamber of the US Congress does the vice-president preside over?
36292.e: The vice-president is also President of the Senate. In the event of a tie, he may cast a vote.
36292.m: The US vice-president also presides over the Senate.

36293.e: A vice-president is the president’s deputy. When the president is not there, the vice-president takes over the duties.
36293.m: The vice-president stands in for the president.

36294.q: Who was the first woman to be Vice-President of the USA?
36294.e: Kamala Harris became the first female Vice-President of the USA in 2021.
36294.m: Kamala Harris was the first female Vice-President of the USA.

36295.q: What does the Vice-President of the Swiss Federal Council usually become the following year?
36295.e: It is customary for the Vice-President of the Federal Council to be elected President the following year.
36295.m: In Switzerland the Vice-President usually soon becomes President.

36296.q: Who was US vice-president for eight years and later became president himself?
36296.e: Joe Biden was vice-president from 2009 to 2017. Then from 2021 to 2025 he was president.
36296.m: Joe Biden was first vice-president and later president.

36297.q: How do the president and vice-president stand for election in the USA?
36297.e: Each party puts forward a team: one person for president and one for vice-president.
36297.m: In the USA the president and vice-president stand as a team.

36298.q: In which country did the people elect a woman as president for the first time in 1980?
36298.e: Vigdís Finnbogadóttir was elected in Iceland in 1980. She was the first female president in the world elected by the people.
36298.m: In 1980 Iceland was the first country to elect a female president.

36299.q: Has Switzerland ever had a female President of the Confederation?
a: No, women may not join the Federal Council
36299.e: Ruth Dreifuss was the first female President of Switzerland in 1999. Since then several women have held this office, for example Doris Leuthard and Simonetta Sommaruga.
36299.m: Switzerland has already had several female Presidents.

36300.q: Who became the first female President of Mexico in 2024?
36300.e: In October 2024 Claudia Sheinbaum took office as the first woman President of Mexico.
36300.m: Claudia Sheinbaum is the first female President of Mexico.

36301.q: Which country got its first female head of government, Sanae Takaichi, in 2025?
36301.e: Sanae Takaichi became Japan’s first female Prime Minister in October 2025.
36301.m: Since 2025 Japan has had a female Prime Minister for the first time.

36302.q: Which country elected the first female president in Africa in 2005?
36302.e: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf won the election in Liberia in 2005 and was president from 2006.
36302.m: Liberia had Africa’s first elected female president.

36303.q: Who was the first woman to lead the government of India?
36303.e: Indira Gandhi became Prime Minister of India in 1966. She was one of the first female heads of government in the world.
36303.m: Indira Gandhi was India’s first female head of government.

36304.q: Who became the first female President of the European Commission in 2019?
36304.e: Since December 2019 Ursula von der Leyen has led the European Commission as the first woman.
36304.m: Ursula von der Leyen is the first woman at the head of the EU Commission.

36306.q: What is the parliament of Germany called?
36306.e: The German parliament is called the German Bundestag. Its members are elected by the people.
